hypotheses/0.description: DED is modeled as a heterogeneous loss-of-homeostasis state. Different combinations of tear-film deficiency, eyelid dysfunction, ocular-surface stress, inflammation, epithelial damage, and neurosensory dysfunction can converge on symptoms; no single downstream node is asserted to be present or dominant in every patient.

evidence.snippet: In a murine DED model, topical administration of MCF for 5 days achieved 84% corneal epithelial recovery and alleviated corneal inflammation and tissue injury.
evidence.explanation: The evidence is explicitly limited to a short murine study, motivating the human-translation gap.

open_questions/0.rationale: The cited efficacy and mechanism data come from a five-day murine DED study. DED is heterogeneous, evaporative forms can have muted inflammation, and CO exposure has a narrow safety context. Translation therefore requires endotype selection, ocular and systemic safety assessment, controlled dose and light-delivery studies, and randomized human efficacy data.

evidence.snippet: In 94% of a cohort of ESCS probands we found mutations in NR2E3 (also known as PNR), which encodes a retinal nuclear receptor recently discovered to be a ligand-dependent transcription factor.
evidence.explanation: Establishes NR2E3 as the causative gene in the large majority of ESCS probands and defines it as a retinal ligand-dependent transcription factor.

evidence.snippet: its physiological activity is essential for proper rod and cone photoreceptor development and maintenance
evidence.explanation: Confirms NR2E3 as a photoreceptor-restricted transcription factor essential for photoreceptor development and maintenance.

evidence.snippet: resulting in the complete deletion of the NR2E3 AF2 domain which is associated with the observed phenotype consistent with retinal degeneration pathway described in Enhanced S-Cone Syndrome (ESCS)
evidence.explanation: Documents a novel homozygous deletion abolishing the NR2E3 AF2 activation domain as a loss-of-function cause of the ESCS phenotype.

steps/1.description: The initiating lesion is biallelic loss of function of NR2E3, which encodes a photoreceptor-specific ligand-dependent nuclear-receptor transcription factor whose expression is restricted to the outer nuclear layer of the retina. NR2E3 normally acts within maturing rod precursors to activate rod genes and to repress the cone (particularly the S-cone) transcriptional program. Pathogenic variants cluster in the conserved DNA-binding and ligand-binding domains; the novel homozygous c.1182del p.(Ile395*) allele deletes the entire NR2E3 AF2 activation domain, abolishing coregulator-dependent transcriptional activity.

evidence.snippet: may result from abnormal cell-fate determination, leading to excess S cones at the expense of other photoreceptor subtypes
evidence.explanation: Directly states the cell-fate-mis-specification mechanism producing excess S cones at the expense of rods and L/M cones.

evidence.snippet: No rods were identified, but cones were increased approximately 2-fold, and 92% were S cones.
evidence.explanation: Postmortem quantification of an ESCS retina confirms rod absence and marked S-cone predominance.

evidence.snippet: The altered ratio of S- to L/M-cone photoreceptor sensitivity in ESCS may be due to abnormal cone cell fate determination during retinal development.
evidence.explanation: Attributes the abnormal S-to-L/M cone ratio to disordered photoreceptor cell-fate determination during retinal development.

steps/2.description: In the absence of NR2E3 repression, the retina overproduces S (blue) cones at the expense of rods and L/M cones. This developmental cell-fate mis-specification is the mechanistic signature that distinguishes ESCS from the rod-first apoptotic pathway of typical retinitis pigmentosa: rather than a mature photoreceptor topography being depleted, the retina is built with an abnormal S-to-L/M cone ratio and a near-absence of rods, and is disorganized from the outset.

evidence.snippet: The clinical phenotype common to all these patients is night blindness, rudimental or absent rod function, and hyperfunction of the "blue" S-cones.
evidence.explanation: Defines the shared NR2E3 phenotype of night blindness with rudimentary or absent rod function and S-cone hyperfunction.

steps/3.description: Because rod precursors are diverted to an S-cone fate, the ESCS retina has rudimentary or absent rod photoreceptors and correspondingly absent scotopic (rod-mediated) function. Clinically this produces lifelong night blindness, typically the earliest symptom, and a non-detectable dark-adapted rod electroretinogram.

evidence.snippet: The retina was also degenerate, retaining photoreceptors in only the central and far peripheral regions.
evidence.explanation: Documents the progressive degenerative loss of photoreceptors in the ESCS retina.

evidence.snippet: People with rod-cone dystrophy (RCD) or enhanced S-cone syndrome (ESCS) have excess fluid under the retina of their eye.
evidence.explanation: Confirms the intraretinal fluid accumulation (macular edema / schisis) that complicates ESCS and threatens central vision.

steps/4.description: Beyond the developmental defect, the ESCS retina undergoes progressive degeneration, retaining photoreceptors only in central and far-peripheral regions over time. Cystoid macular edema and intraretinal schisis cysts are frequent complications (the Goldmann-Favre end of the spectrum), causing additional loss of central vision.

evidence.snippet: People with ESCS also suffer visual loss, with night blindness occurring from early in life
evidence.explanation: Directly reports early-onset night blindness as a cardinal ESCS phenotype.

steps/5.description: Rudimentary or absent rod function produces nyctalopia from early in life, typically the earliest presenting symptom of ESCS.

edges/1.description: Loss of NR2E3 transcriptional activity removes the repression of the S-cone program in rod-committed precursors, redirecting photoreceptor cell fate.

edges/2.description: Redirection of rod precursors toward an S-cone fate leaves the retina with rudimentary or absent rod photoreceptors.

edges/3.description: The dysplastic, disorganized photoreceptor mosaic is intrinsically unstable and undergoes progressive degeneration over time.

edges/4.description: Rod deficiency abolishes scotopic vision, producing nyctalopia from early life.

evidence.snippet: In 16 ESCS patients with the most common NR2E3 mutation, R311Q, we documented an abnormal ratio of S to L/M cone function
evidence.explanation: Identifies R311Q as the most common NR2E3 mutation in ESCS.

evidence.snippet: A high proportion of mutations are located in the evolutionarily-conserved DNA-binding domains (DBDs) and ligand-binding domains (LBDs) of NR2E3.
evidence.explanation: Localizes the majority of pathogenic NR2E3 variants to the conserved DBD and LBD.

evidence.snippet: Genetic analysis identified a novel homozygous deletion in NR2E3 gene: Chr15(GRCh37): g.71817633del c.1182del p. (Ile395*) resulting in the complete deletion of the NR2E3 AF2 domain
evidence.explanation: Reports a novel homozygous AF2-domain-deleting NR2E3 variant causing ESCS.

genes/0.notes: ESCS is caused by biallelic NR2E3 variants. The recurrent p.Arg311Gln (R311Q) ligand-binding-domain substitution is the most common ESCS allele; pathogenic variants concentrate in the conserved DNA-binding and ligand-binding domains. A novel homozygous c.1182del p.(Ile395*) deleting the AF2 activation domain has also been reported. The single dominant p.Gly56Arg allele causes autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa rather than ESCS.

treatments/0.description: Topical or systemic carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (e.g., acetazolamide, dorzolamide) are used to reduce the cystoid macular edema and intraretinal schisis that complicate ESCS, aiming to preserve central vision. There is no treatment that reverses the underlying photoreceptor cell-fate defect.

evidence.snippet: The medicine interferon gamma-1b may help people with these diseases.
evidence.explanation: The trial evaluates topical interferon gamma-1b for the macular edema/schisis of ESCS.

treatments/1.description: Topical interferon gamma-1b eyedrops have been evaluated in an early-phase (Phase I/II) trial to reduce macular edema and intraretinal schisis cysts in ESCS and rod-cone dystrophy.

treatments/2.description: Management is largely supportive: low-vision aids and rehabilitation, monitoring for maculopathy, and genetic counseling for this autosomal recessive disorder.

evidence.snippet: Ewing sarcomas are driven by EWS-ETS fusions, most commonly EWS-FLI1, which promotes widespread metabolic reprogramming, including activation of serine biosynthesis.
evidence.explanation: This supports EWS-FLI1 as a key driver fusion in Ewing sarcoma, but not all specific structural details in the descriptor.

evidence.snippet: It is associated in 85% of cases with the t(11;22)(q24:q12) chromosomal translocation that generates fusion of the 5' segment of the EWS gene with the 3' segment of the ETS family gene FLI-1.
evidence.explanation: Directly supports the 85% frequency of EWS-FLI1 translocation and its structural details.

evidence.snippet: The resulting EWS-FLI-1 fusion protein is believed to behave as an aberrant transcriptional activator that contributes to ESFT development by altering the expression of its target genes in a permissive cellular environment.
evidence.explanation: Supports the role of EWS-FLI1 as an aberrant transcription factor driving tumor development.

steps/1.description: The t(11;22)(q24;q12) translocation fuses the EWS gene (EWSR1) on chromosome 22 with the FLI1 gene on chromosome 11. The resulting EWS-FLI1 protein functions as an aberrant FET-ETS transcription factor. It is the truncal driver of most Ewing sarcomas, but its oncogenic effect depends on a permissive developmental cell state and on downstream enhancer, transcriptional, metabolic, and DNA damage-response programs.

evidence.snippet: Using biochemical assays and epigenomics, we show that ETV6 competes with EWS-FLI1 for binding to select DNA elements enriched for short GGAA repeat sequences.
evidence.explanation: Supports ETV6 competition with EWS-FLI1 at short GGAA-repeat elements.

evidence.snippet: Recent studies identified ETV6 as a vulnerability in Ewing sarcoma, where it competes with EWS::FLI1 at short GGAA repeats to restrain EWS::FLI1 function.
evidence.explanation: Supports ETV6 as a restraining factor and therapeutic vulnerability.

evidence.snippet: Upon inactivating ETV6, EWS-FLI1 overtakes and hyper-activates these cis-elements to promote mesenchymal differentiation, with SOX11 being a key downstream target.
evidence.explanation: ETV6 loss releases fusion occupancy at selected sites and promotes differentiation rather than uniformly reversing all fusion activity.

steps/2.description: ETV6 is a native ETS-family factor that competes with EWS-FLI1 at select short GGAA-repeat elements. This counter-regulatory layer restrains part of the enhanceropathy, and forced ETV6 degradation can paradoxically increase EWS-FLI1 transcriptional stress and tumor cell death.

evidence.snippet: At rs79965208, the A risk allele connected adjacent GGAA repeats by converting an interspaced GGAT motif into a GGAA motif, thereby increasing the number of consecutive GGAA motifs and thus the EWSR1-FLI1-dependent enhancer activity of this sequence, with epigenetic characteristics of an active regulatory element.
evidence.explanation: Supports the mechanism by which a germline risk allele creates a stronger GGAA enhancer at EGR2.

evidence.snippet: EWSR1-FLI1 preferentially bound to the A risk allele, which increased global and allele-specific EGR2 expression.
evidence.explanation: Supports allele-specific EWS-FLI1 binding at a germline susceptibility repeat.

evidence.snippet: We identified 50 microsatellite alleles at 6p25.1 and observed that EwS-affected individuals had longer alleles (>135 bp) with more GGAA repeats.
evidence.explanation: Supports longer germline GGAA alleles in Ewing sarcoma cases at the RREB1-associated susceptibility locus.

evidence.snippet: RREB1 knockdown reduced proliferation and clonogenic potential and reduced expression of cell cycle and DNA replication genes.
evidence.explanation: Links the RREB1 susceptibility enhancer mechanism to proliferation and clonogenic growth.

steps/3.description: Germline variation in GGAA microsatellite architecture can determine how strongly the acquired EWS-FLI1 fusion converts a locus into a neo-enhancer. At EGR2 and RREB1 susceptibility loci, longer or newly contiguous GGAA repeat alleles increase EWS-FLI1 binding and enhancer output, linking inherited repeat length to the somatic enhanceropathy and proliferative transcriptional programs.

evidence.snippet: We report that transient exposure to IGF-1 concentrations mimicking serum levels during puberty reprograms limb-derived mesenchymal cells of EWS::FLI1-mutant mice to stable transformation and tumorigenicity.
evidence.explanation: Supports pubertal-level IGF-1 exposure as a cooperating developmental signal.

evidence.snippet: We identify a modular mechanism of IGF-1-driven tumor promotion in the early steps of EwS pathogenesis, in which Yap1 plays a central role.
evidence.explanation: Supports YAP1 as the central mediator of the IGF-1 cooperating mechanism.

steps/4.description: Transient IGF-1 exposure at concentrations chosen to mimic pubertal serum levels reprogrammed limb-derived mesenchymal cells from EWS-FLI1-mutant mice through a YAP1-centered mechanism and enabled stable tumorigenicity. This model suggests a developmental cooperating signal but does not establish puberty as the time of human initiation, a universal IGF-1 requirement, or a human cell of origin. YAP1/TAZ can oppose fusion transcription while promoting aggressive behavior in established tumors, so initiation and maintenance contexts require separate testing.

evidence.snippet: Although CHD4 and NuRD colocalized with EWS-FLI1 at enhancers and super-enhancers, CHD4 promoted Ewing sarcoma cell survival not by modulating EWS-FLI1 activity and its oncogenic gene expression program but by regulating chromatin structure.
evidence.explanation: Separates CHD4 structural maintenance from EWS-FLI1 target-gene repression.

evidence.snippet: CHD4 depletion led to a global increase in DNA accessibility and induction of spontaneous DNA damage, resulting in an increased susceptibility to DNA-damaging agents.
evidence.explanation: Links chromatin architecture maintenance to protection from spontaneous damage.

steps/5.description: CHD4/NuRD maintains global chromatin structure and limits spontaneous DNA damage in Ewing cells. Despite colocalization with EWS-FLI1 at enhancers, the reported survival effect did not operate by changing EWS-FLI1 activity or its oncogenic expression program. CHD4 loss causes apoptosis and increases sensitivity to DNA-damaging agents; combined CHD4 depletion and olaparib suppressed xenograft growth.

evidence.snippet: Although the histogenesis of ESFT is controversial, mesenchymal (MSC) and/or neural crest (NCSC) stem cells have been implicated as cells of origin.
evidence.explanation: Supports the leading mesenchymal and neural crest cell-of-origin hypotheses.

evidence.snippet: Together these studies confirm that, unlike terminally differentiated cells but consistent with bone marrow-derived MSC, NCSC tolerate expression of EWS-FLI1 and ectopic expression of the oncogene initiates transition to an ESFT-like state.
evidence.explanation: Supports the ability of EWS-FLI1 to initiate an Ewing-like state in neural crest-related cells.

evidence.snippet: Ewing sarcoma (ES) is an aggressive bone and soft tissue neoplasm characterized by EWSR::ETS rearrangements whose cellular origin remains unclear.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the unresolved nature of the cell-of-origin question.

evidence.snippet: Xenografting of EWS::FLI1-transduced heMSCs results in the formation of tumors expressing characteristic ES markers.
evidence.explanation: Supports the embryonic mesenchymal stem-cell transformation model in xenografts.

evidence.snippet: Neural crest-derived cells uniquely tolerate expression of EWSR1::FLI1, and targeted expression of EWSR1::FLI1 in these cells generates lethal Ewing sarcomas.
evidence.explanation: Lineage-specific tolerance and tumor formation in zebrafish support a neural crest origin in this model, not definitive human ancestry.

steps/6.description: The human cell of origin remains unresolved. Human neural crest-derived stem cells can tolerate EWS-FLI1, and early human embryonic mesenchymal cells can acquire an Ewing-like program and form xenografts. A zebrafish genetic model demonstrates neural crest-to-mesoderm reprogramming and tumors after lineage-targeted fusion expression. These experiments identify permissive states in distinct systems; neither molecular similarity nor engineered transformation uniquely traces the origin of human tumors.

evidence.snippet: Here, we demonstrate that these same biophysical cues-modeled by coculturing ES cells and mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) in 3D scaffolds within a flow perfusion bioreactor-activate interleukin-6 and transcription factor Stat3.
evidence.explanation: A tissue-engineered tumor-stroma coculture demonstrates IL-6/STAT3 activation under biophysical stimulation.

steps/7.description: In flow-perfusion coculture, mesenchymal stromal cells and Ewing tumor cells respond to biophysical cues through IL-6/STAT3 signaling and altered drug response. This established-tumor microenvironment mechanism is distinct from IGF-1/YAP1 developmental initiation.

evidence.snippet: We demonstrate that PSaRC318 cells, a novel patient-derived cell line harboring a pathogenic BARD1 variant, are sensitive to PARP inhibition and by testing the effect of BARD1 depletion in additional Ewing sarcoma cell lines, we confirm that BARD1 loss enhances cell sensitivity to PARP inhibition plus radiation.
evidence.explanation: Patient-derived and BARD1-depleted cell models support an experimental modifier, not a validated patient biomarker or a ten-percent BARD1 frequency.

evidence.snippet: Here, we demonstrate that GBP1 contributes to the enhanced sensitivity of BARD1 deficient Ewing cells to DNA damage.
evidence.explanation: GBP1 knockdown reduced radiation- and niraparib-associated apoptosis in PSaRC318 cells; GBP1 expression is not specific to BARD1 loss.

steps/8.description: A BARD1-variant patient-derived Ewing cell line and BARD1-depletion experiments show enhanced sensitivity to PARP inhibition and radiation. BARD1 loss can increase GBP1 expression, which contributes to damage-induced apoptosis in the tested cells. Other signals also induce GBP1, so expression is not a specific BARD1-loss marker. This is a bounded experimental modifier of treatment response; neither disease-wide BARD1 prevalence, penetrant inherited Ewing susceptibility nor a validated clinical predictive biomarker is established.

evidence.snippet: In Ewing sarcoma, we find that the BAF complex is recruited by the EWS-FLI1 fusion protein to tumor-specific enhancers and contributes to target gene activation.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates that EWS-FLI1 recruits BAF complexes to tumor-specific enhancers and that this recruitment contributes to gene activation.

evidence.snippet: This process is a neomorphic property of EWS-FLI1 compared to wild-type FLI1 and depends on tyrosine residues that are necessary for phase transitions of the EWSR1 prion-like domain.
evidence.explanation: Supports the phase-transition/prion-like-domain component of BAF retargeting by EWS-FLI1.

steps/9.description: EWS-FLI1 uses the EWSR1 low-complexity/prion-like domain to retarget BRG1/BRM-associated factor (BAF/SWI-SNF) chromatin-remodeling complexes to tumor-specific enhancers. This neomorphic recruitment depends on tyrosine residues linked to phase-transition behavior of the EWSR1 domain and helps establish oncogenic enhancer activity.

evidence.snippet: We found that endogenous EWS::FLI1 forms dynamic, sub-diffraction-limit hubs with mechanisms of dissolution that prevent the hubs from achieving macroscopic liquid-liquid phase separation.
evidence.explanation: Endogenous live-cell imaging in a bioRxiv preprint supports dynamic hubs; peer-reviewed replication is still needed.

evidence.snippet: Quantitative single-cell and single-molecule imaging reveals that the oncogenic TF EWS::FLI1 requires a narrow optimum of LCD-LCD interactions to activate its target genes associated with GGAA microsatellites.
evidence.explanation: Supports a narrow low-complexity-domain interaction window for oncogenic transcription.

steps/10.description: EWS-FLI1 low-complexity-domain interactions support GGAA-associated transcription within a narrow interaction-strength optimum. A 2026 bioRxiv preprint reports endogenous dynamic sub-diffraction hubs that dissolve before macroscopic liquid-liquid phase separation. This is a provisional refinement of the published interaction-optimum model, not evidence that macroscopic condensates are required for oncogenesis.

evidence.snippet: Mechanistic studies demonstrate that the NuRD co-repressor complex interacts with EWS/FLI, and that its associated histone deacetylase and LSD1 activities contribute to the repressive function.
evidence.explanation: Biochemical and functional experiments establish the NuRD-associated repressive arm.

evidence.snippet: Here, we demonstrate that a previously less-well characterized transcriptional repressive function of the EWS/FLI fusion is also required for the transformed phenotype of Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.explanation: Repression is functionally required in the tested Ewing cell models.

steps/11.description: EWS-FLI1 recruits NuRD-associated HDAC and LSD1 activities to repress tumor-suppressive and lineage-regulatory genes. Repression contributes to transformation alongside enhancer activation. CHD4 also maintains global chromatin architecture and survival, but this distinct dependency should not be equated with regulation of EWS-FLI1 transcriptional output.

evidence.snippet: We identified and validated an EWS-FLI1 binding site at the ATF4 promoter, indicating that the fusion can directly activate ATF4 transcription.
evidence.explanation: Supports direct fusion-driven ATF4 activation.

evidence.snippet: Here, we demonstrate that EWS-FLI1 positively regulates the expression of proteins required for serine-glycine biosynthesis and uptake of the alternative nutrient source glutamine.
evidence.explanation: Supports direct EWS-FLI1 control of serine-glycine biosynthesis and glutamine uptake.

evidence.snippet: In summary, our study demonstrates that EWS-FLI1 reprograms the metabolism of EWS cells and that serine-glycine metabolism or glutamine uptake are potential targetable vulnerabilities in this tumor type.
evidence.explanation: Supports the therapeutic-vulnerability interpretation of this metabolic mechanism.

steps/12.description: EWS-FLI1 and menin converge on ATF4 to activate a serine synthesis pathway transcriptional program. EWS-FLI1 also upregulates glutamine uptake and one-carbon cycle genes, linking fusion-driven transcription to biosynthetic metabolism, redox state, and survival.

evidence.snippet: We discovered that EWS::FLI1 prevents the resolution of R-loops induced by these drugs via sequestering DHX9 helicase, ultimately resulting in R-loop accumulation, replication stress, and genome instability.
evidence.explanation: Supports the direct DHX9-sequestration arm of the R-loop mechanism.

steps/13.description: Following topoisomerase I poison exposure, EWS-FLI1 sequesters DHX9 helicase and prevents resolution of drug-induced R-loops. Excess DHX9 or reduced fusion expression confers SN-38 resistance independent of measured proliferation and global transcription rates. This supports a protein-interaction contribution under topoisomerase stress, without proving complete independence from transcription or untreated tumor initiation.

evidence.snippet: Here we show that Ewing sarcoma cells display alterations in regulation of damage-induced transcription, accumulation of R-loops and increased replication stress.
evidence.explanation: Supports R-loop accumulation and replication stress downstream of EWS-FLI1 activity.

steps/14.description: EWS-FLI1-driven transcription and impaired regulation of damage-induced transcription promote RNA:DNA hybrids and replication stress in Ewing cell models. The stress state creates DNA-damage vulnerabilities and dependence on buffering pathways. It does not itself cause enhanced survival, and it is not synonymous with a uniform BRCA-mutant clinical phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Strikingly, in STAG2 knockout cells the oncogenic genetic program driven by the fusion transcription factor EWS/FLI1 was highly perturbed, in part due to altered enhancer-promoter contacts. Moreover, loss of STAG2 also disrupted PRC2-mediated regulation of gene expression.
evidence.explanation: Supports STAG2 loss as a chromatin and transcriptional rewiring mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Finally, consistent with clinical observations, functional studies revealed that loss of STAG2 enhances the metastatic potential of Ewing sarcoma xenografts.
evidence.explanation: Supports the metastasis-promoting consequence in xenograft models.

evidence.snippet: Together, these findings reveal that STAG2 loss reprograms, rather than globally attenuates, EWS-FLI1 function, amplifying a high-risk oncogenic transcriptional state in Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.explanation: Supports the current model that STAG2 loss changes the quality of EWS-FLI1 enhancer activity.

evidence.snippet: Subsequent genomic profiling and high-resolution chromatin interaction data from Capture Hi-C indicated that cohesin-STAG2 facilitates communication between EWS::FLI1-bound long GGAA repeats, presumably acting as neoenhancers, and their target promoters.
evidence.explanation: Supports STAG2/cohesin control of long-GGAA neo-enhancer to promoter communication.

evidence.snippet: Changes in CTCF-dependent chromatin contacts involving signature genes, unrelated to EWS::FLI1 binding, were also identified.
evidence.explanation: Supports an EWS-FLI1-independent CTCF-contact arm of STAG2 loss.

evidence.snippet: Among patients with localised disease, 5-year event-free survival was 54% (95% CI 34-70%) and 75% (95% CI 63-84%) for patients with STAG2 loss vs. expression (P = 0.0034).
evidence.explanation: Supports adverse clinical prognosis associated with STAG2 protein loss in localized Ewing sarcoma.

evidence.snippet: In an expanded cohort of 299 patients with clinical data, we discovered that STAG2 and TP53 mutations are often concurrent and are associated with poor outcome.
evidence.explanation: Supports the high-risk STAG2/TP53 co-alteration component of the model.

evidence.snippet: cannot be replaced by the SA1-containing cohesin complex (cohesin-SA1) when SA2 is absent
evidence.explanation: Supplies the paralog non-compensation premise this node depends on: losing STAG2 is not buffered by cohesin-SA1 at the affected sites. Established in general human cells, not in Ewing sarcoma.

evidence.snippet: cohesin-SA2 promotes cell-type-specific contacts between enhancers and promoters independently of CTCF
evidence.explanation: Identifies the CTCF-independent enhancer-promoter contact function of cohesin-SA2, which is the function the EWS-FLI1 neo-enhancer arm of this node assumes is lost. It does not itself show that loss at GGAA repeats.

evidence.snippet: identified STAG1 as the most prominent and selective dependency of STAG2-deficient cells
evidence.explanation: Supports a STAG1-directed synthetic-lethal vulnerability created by the STAG2-altered state. Demonstrated by genome-wide screens in isogenic cancer cell lines generally, not in Ewing sarcoma models, and not tested clinically in this disease. This is distinct from the replication-fork route already cited from broader cancer models.

steps/15.description: STAG2 loss remodels cohesin-dependent enhancer-promoter and CTCF contacts and perturbs PRC2-regulated programs in a subset of Ewing tumors. A recent study found loss of many short-GGAA binding sites with increased fusion occupancy and activity at multimeric repeats. Earlier work showed that STAG2 normally facilitates long-GGAA enhancer contacts; this is related evidence, not an independent replication of the same directional occupancy change. STAG2 protein loss and STAG2/TP53 co-mutation associate with adverse outcome in specific cohorts, but mutation, protein loss and inferred chromatin states are not interchangeable biomarkers. Paralog non-compensation is why losing STAG2 has an enhancer-specific consequence at all: cohesin-SA2 occupies a population of CTCF-free enhancers that cohesin-SA1 does not take over in its absence. The same paralog relationship makes STAG1 a selective dependency of STAG2-deficient cells. Both results come from general human cell and isogenic cancer-line systems rather than Ewing sarcoma models, so they supply the underlying cohesin biology and a candidate vulnerability, not an Ewing-specific or clinically tested one.

evidence.snippet: Mechanistically, TRIM8 knockout led to an increase in EWS/FLI protein levels that was not tolerated.
evidence.explanation: CRISPR perturbation links TRIM8-mediated fusion turnover to a tolerated protein-abundance window.

evidence.snippet: Strikingly, modest EF depletion promoted a pro-metastatic phenotype that diminished upon near-complete EF loss, revealing a paradoxical effect of submaximal EF inhibition.
evidence.explanation: Graded depletion in engineered preclinical models produces a non-monotonic phenotype; it does not demonstrate metastasis induced by partial drug inhibition in patients.

evidence.snippet: In EwS tumors, cell proliferation and strong oxidative phosphorylation metabolism are associated with a well-defined range of EWSR1-FLI1 activity.
evidence.explanation: Gives the dosage window a readout in patient tumors rather than only in engineered models: proliferation and oxidative phosphorylation track a bounded range of inferred fusion activity. Activity is inferred from a transcriptional signature, so this does not measure fusion protein abundance.

evidence.snippet: a subpopulation of cells from below and above the intermediary EWSR1-FLI1 activity is characterized by increased hypoxia
evidence.explanation: Supports the non-monotonic shape of the window independently of the depletion experiments: cells on both sides of the intermediate range adopt a hypoxia program rather than simply losing proliferative output.

steps/16.description: Fusion abundance and low-complexity-domain interaction strength are related but distinct control variables. TRIM8-mediated turnover prevents toxic fusion accumulation. Engineered graded depletion and restoration of endogenous EWS-FLI1 produce persistent transcriptional changes and increased metastatic behavior at intermediate depletion in preclinical models. This does not establish a clinical hazard of a particular inhibitor dose. Independently of those engineered perturbations, single-cell profiling of patient tumors associates an intermediate range of inferred fusion activity with proliferation and oxidative phosphorylation, and cells on either side of that range with a hypoxia program. That is a cross-sectional association in tumors, not a demonstration that fusion dose sets the program.

evidence.snippet: In addition, homologous recombination is impaired in Ewing sarcoma owing to an enriched interaction between BRCA1 and the elongating transcription machinery.
evidence.explanation: Supports BRCA1 sequestration and impaired HR in the studied Ewing models.

evidence.snippet: Here, we show that PARP inhibitor sensitivity in Ewing's sarcoma cells is not through an apparent defect in DNA repair by HR, but through hypersensitivity to trapped PARP1-DNA complexes.
evidence.explanation: A separate cellular study found HR proficiency and implicated PARP trapping; differences in assays and conditions remain relevant.

steps/17.description: Enrichment of BRCA1 at elongating transcription machinery can reduce its availability for damage repair in Ewing cell models. Other experiments found no apparent HR defect and attributed PARP sensitivity to trapped PARP-DNA complexes. These observations constrain the scope of an HR-deficiency model rather than establishing either uniform HR proficiency or uniform clinical BRCAness. PARP trapping and context-dependent HR impairment can coexist.

evidence.snippet: EWS-FLI1 binds near the transcription start site of SLFN11 promoter and acts as a positive regulator of SLFN11 expression in Ewing sarcoma cells.
evidence.explanation: Direct promoter binding and expression perturbation support fusion-driven SLFN11 transcription.

evidence.snippet: Unlike ATR, SLFN11 neither interferes with the loading of CDC45 and PCNA nor inhibits the initiation of DNA replication but selectively blocks fork progression while inducing chromatin opening across replication initiation sites.
evidence.explanation: Mechanistic fork-blocking experiments in cancer cell models provide complementary, not exclusively Ewing-specific, support.

steps/18.description: EWS-FLI1 directly increases SLFN11 expression. SLFN11 blocks stressed replication forks and promotes susceptibility to DNA-damaging agents. Expression-outcome correlations are not a validated standalone clinical selection test. Loss of SLFN11 can confer treatment resistance and is associated with metabolic adaptation in Ewing models.

evidence.snippet: Together, our study demonstrates that USP1 is regulated by EWS::FLI1, the USP1-Survivin axis promotes EWS cell survival, and USP1 inhibition sensitizes cells to standard of care chemotherapy.
evidence.explanation: Ewing cellular experiments support a distinct fusion-regulated stress-buffering pathway.

steps/19.description: EWS-FLI1 increases USP1 expression. USP1 stabilizes survivin and buffers replication-stress-associated apoptosis, allowing continued Ewing cell survival. USP1 inhibition sensitizes cells to doxorubicin and etoposide in preclinical experiments; human efficacy has not been established.

evidence.snippet: Expression of EWS-FLI1, or loss of EWSR1, causes exon 25 skipping of the POLQ transcript, decreased POLΘ expression, impaired MMEJ, and cellular sensitivity to inhibitors of the Fanconi Anemia (FA), NHEJ, or HR pathways, through the mechanism of synthetic lethality.
evidence.explanation: A 2025 bioRxiv preprint reports altered POLQ splicing and rescue experiments. This remains provisional and does not establish efficacy of the proposed inhibitors in patients.

steps/20.description: A 2025 bioRxiv preprint reports that EWS-FLI1 expression or EWSR1 loss induces POLQ exon 25 skipping, reduces polymerase theta protein, and impairs microhomology-mediated end joining. Fusion knockdown and POLQ rescue support causality in tested models. Proposed synthetic lethality with other repair pathways requires independent replication and clinical evaluation; this is an emerging additional repair defect rather than a reason to erase the BRCA1 literature.

evidence.snippet: Here, we leverage transcriptomic and metabolomic profiling in patient-derived EWS models to demonstrate that SLFN11 loss drives downregulated mitochondrial glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GPD2) expression, higher accumulation of glycerol-3-phosphate, fatty acid unsaturation, and enhanced glycerophospholipid (GPL) biosynthesis.
evidence.explanation: SLFN11 knockout and multi-omics support lipid remodeling in Ewing models. The molecular route to GPD2 suppression was not resolved.

steps/21.description: SLFN11-deficient Ewing models show reduced GPD2 expression and increased glycerophospholipid biosynthesis. Pharmacologic inhibition of glycerophospholipid synthesis increased SN-38 sensitivity in vitro, with modest and cell-line-dependent combination effects. The regulatory link from SLFN11 loss to GPD2 suppression and human predictive value remain unresolved. This loss state is not represented as a positive consequence of SLFN11 fork arrest.

evidence.snippet: Notably, EWS-FLI1 fusion genes acted in a positive feedback loop to maintain the expression of PARP1, which was required for EWS-FLI-mediated transcription, thereby enforcing oncogene-dependent sensitivity to PARP-1 inhibition.
evidence.explanation: Ewing cellular studies support reciprocal dependence of fusion transcription and PARP1.

steps/22.description: PARP1 interacts with EWS-FLI1 and EWS-ERG and supports fusion-mediated transcription; EWS-FLI1 also maintains PARP1 expression. This experimentally reported feedback connects transcription and damage response. The preclinical drug rationale has not translated into uniform clinical response.

evidence.snippet: We find that EWS-FLI1 reprograms gene regulatory circuits in Ewing sarcoma by directly inducing or repressing enhancers.
evidence.explanation: Directly supports enhancer-level reprogramming as a central EWS-FLI1 mechanism.

evidence.snippet: At GGAA repeat elements, which lack evolutionary conservation and regulatory potential in other cell types, EWS-FLI1 multimers induce chromatin opening and create de novo enhancers that physically interact with target promoters.
evidence.explanation: Supports GGAA-repeat enhancer creation and chromatin opening.

evidence.snippet: We found that in tumor cells, EWS-FLI targets regions of the genome distinct from FLI1, despite identical DNA-binding domains.
evidence.explanation: Supports Ian Davis lab evidence that the fusion retargets chromatin differently from wild-type FLI1.

evidence.snippet: Expression of EWS-FLI results in nucleosome depletion at targeted sites, whereas silencing of EWS-FLI in tumor cells restored nucleosome occupancy.
evidence.explanation: Supports the chromatin-accessibility arm of the EWS-FLI1 enhanceropathy.

evidence.snippet: EWS-FLI1 engages GGAA microsatellite repeats to form de novo enhancers that activate oncogenic transcriptional programs essential for tumorigenesis.
evidence.explanation: Confirms the GGAA microsatellite enhancer mechanism in a recent STAG2-focused study.

evidence.snippet: We observed consistent DNA hypomethylation at enhancers regulated by the disease-defining EWS-FLI1 fusion protein, thus establishing epigenomic enhancer reprogramming as a ubiquitous and characteristic feature of Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.explanation: Supports enhancer reprogramming as a recurrent epigenomic feature in patient tumors.

steps/23.description: EWS-FLI1 binds GGAA microsatellite repeats and canonical ETS motifs, remodeling the enhancer landscape. At GGAA repeats, multimeric EWS-FLI1 opens chromatin and creates de novo enhancers that contact target promoters; at conserved ETS enhancers, EWS-FLI1 can displace wild-type ETS factors and repress tumor suppressor and lineage-regulatory programs.

evidence.snippet: Epigenomic analyses demonstrate that EWS-FLI1, the primary fusion driver for this cancer, directly establishes super-enhancers of each of these three TFs to activate their transcription.
evidence.explanation: Supports direct establishment of KLF15, TCF4, and NKX2-2 super-enhancers by EWS-FLI1.

evidence.snippet: Functionally, CRC factors contribute significantly to cell proliferation of Ewing sarcoma both in vitro and in vivo.
evidence.explanation: Supports the downstream proliferation role of the core regulatory circuitry.

steps/24.description: EWS-FLI1 activates super-enhancers controlling a core regulatory circuitry composed of transcription factors including KLF15, TCF4, and NKX2-2. These factors reinforce their own and each other's regulatory elements and cooperate with EWS-FLI1 to sustain proliferation, survival signaling, and the Ewing transcriptional state.

steps/25.description: Multiple fusion-driven mechanisms converge on tumor cell proliferation and survival: core regulatory circuitry sustains oncogenic signaling, metabolic reprogramming supplies biomass and redox buffering, and replication-stress adaptation prevents apoptosis during genotoxic stress.

evidence.snippet: In ES of the bone, plain radiographs exhibit permeative and infiltrative destruction of the affected bone
evidence.explanation: Clinical imaging review supports a destructive osseous growth mechanism, distinct from extraskeletal disease.

steps/26.description: In osseous Ewing sarcoma, infiltrative tumor growth destroys the affected bone and can extend through cortex into soft tissue. Local structural injury contributes to pain, swelling and fracture risk. These consequences are specific to osseous or bone-involving disease; treatment can also contribute to later fractures.

evidence.snippet: Here, we found EWS/FLI1 bound to the EZH2 promoter in vivo, and induced EZH2 expression in ET and mesenchymal stem cells.
evidence.explanation: Chromatin binding and expression experiments support fusion-associated EZH2 induction; in vivo here describes binding within cells, not an animal efficacy result.

evidence.snippet: Subsequent microarray analysis of EZH2 knock down, HDAC-inhibitor treatment and confirmation in independent assays revealed an undifferentiated phenotype maintained by EZH2 in ET.
evidence.explanation: Cellular perturbation supports maintenance of an undifferentiated transcriptional state.

steps/27.description: EWS-FLI1 induces EZH2, which contributes to repression of differentiation-associated genes and maintenance of an undifferentiated state. Genetic depletion impairs clonogenicity and tumorigenicity in preclinical systems. This dependency is distinct from the heterogeneous PRC2 changes following STAG2 loss and does not imply that every Ewing tumor will respond to an EZH2 inhibitor.

evidence.snippet: Here we provide evidence that NKX2-2 mediates the EWS/FLI-controlled block of mesenchymal features.
evidence.explanation: Directly supports EWS/FLI-mediated repression of mesenchymal features and blocked differentiation programs.

evidence.snippet: These divergent chromatin-remodeling patterns repress tumor suppressors and mesenchymal lineage regulators while activating oncogenes and potential therapeutic targets, such as the kinase VRK1.
evidence.explanation: Supports enhancer-level repression of mesenchymal lineage regulators.

steps/28.description: EWS-FLI1 and its downstream transcriptional circuitry repress mesenchymal lineage regulators, maintaining Ewing sarcoma cells in an immature, proliferative state. This mechanism is linked to the unresolved cell-of-origin question because only some early progenitor contexts tolerate EWS-FLI1 and progress toward an Ewing-like state.

evidence.snippet: We found that EWS::FLI1 creates a de novo GGAA microsatellite enhancer in a developmentally conserved regulatory region of the HOXD locus.
evidence.explanation: Enhancer perturbation supports fusion-dependent HOXD locus activation.

evidence.snippet: More strikingly, HOXD13 bound and activated EWS::FLI1-repressed genes, leading to adoption of mesenchymal and migratory cell states that are normally suppressed by the fusion.
evidence.explanation: Supports transcriptional antagonism and a mesenchymal-state modifier rather than uniformly blocked differentiation.

steps/29.description: Fusion-created enhancer activity at the HOXD locus induces a developmental transcriptional program. HOXD13 activates some genes normally repressed by EWS-FLI1 and shifts cells toward mesenchymal and migratory states. This provides a defined modifier of the differentiation block and contributes to a continuum of tumor states.

evidence.snippet: When we examined primary EwS patient tumors, we observed these same regulatory modules were variably enriched both across and within tumors, highlighting the existence of intratumoral heterogeneity in gene regulatory networks.
evidence.explanation: Single-cell RNA/ATAC analyses identify multiple coexisting regulatory programs rather than a single binary fusion-high/fusion-low axis.

evidence.snippet: These cells retained expression of the fusion-activated gene signature alongside high expression of genes that are normally repressed by EWS::FLI1.
evidence.explanation: CD73-positive CAF-like tumor cells can occupy hybrid transcriptional states; they are malignant cells, not automatically nonmalignant fibroblasts.

evidence.snippet: Thus, these EwS cells gained mesenchymal properties, including the capacity to deposit ECM, without losing proliferative or tumorigenic potential.
evidence.explanation: The source directly links the hybrid malignant-cell state to extracellular-matrix deposition. The annotation does not relabel these malignant cells as ordinary fibroblasts.

steps/30.description: Ewing tumors contain coexisting gene-regulatory programs. CD73-positive malignant subpopulations can retain fusion-activated genes while expressing normally repressed mesenchymal and extracellular-matrix genes. These CAF-like tumor cells deposit matrix near tumor borders and invasive foci. Their presence is not proof of a separate fibroblast lineage, and a universal binary fusion-high/fusion-low switch does not capture the observed heterogeneity.

evidence.snippet: Pain (75.3%) was the most common symptom at presentation.
evidence.explanation: A 73-patient cohort restricted to adults reported pain in 75.3%; this supports the within-cohort frequency and common clinical presentation.

steps/31.description: Localized bone pain is a common presenting symptom of osseous disease, sometimes intermittent or initially attributed to strain. Frequency varies with age, site and ascertainment; the cited 75.3% estimate is from a single-center adult cohort, not a universal pediatric estimate.

evidence.snippet: In this study, pain and swelling were the most common presenting complaints seen in 75.3% and 42.5% patients, respectively
evidence.explanation: Adult single-center cohort supports swelling as a common presentation; no universal VERY_FREQUENT estimate is inferred.

steps/32.description: A palpable mass or localized swelling may develop as tumor extends through the bone cortex into surrounding soft tissues. The mass is often firm and may be tender or warm, and may initially be attributed to trauma or infection.

evidence.snippet: Among 21 (28.8%) patients, the lung (61.9%) was the most common site of metastasis followed by the bone, bone marrow, and brain.
evidence.explanation: Supports the OCCASIONAL frequency band (5-29%) for metastatic disease at presentation — 28.8% of this 73-patient cohort presented with metastases — and the stated pattern of spread to lung, bone, and bone marrow. This is the frequency evidence; the survival items below support the separate prognostic claim, not the frequency.

evidence.snippet: The 3-year EFS estimates were 37.4% (95% CI, 29.3 to 45.5) for the standard arm and 39.1% (95% CI, 31.3 to 46.7) for the experimental arm (stratified EFS-event hazard ratio for experimental arm 1.00; 95% CI, 0.76 to 1.33; 1-sided, P = .50).
evidence.explanation: Provides precise 3-year EFS data from the COG AEWS1221 phase III trial for metastatic Ewing sarcoma.

evidence.snippet: Although only 25% of patients have obvious metastases at diagnosis
evidence.explanation: The contemporary guideline supports the approximate presentation frequency.

steps/33.description: About one quarter of patients have detectable metastases at diagnosis, predominantly in lung, bone and bone marrow. Prognosis depends on metastatic distribution, age and treatment. In the metastatic AEWS1221 trial, three-year event-free survival was 37.4% with VDC/IE and 39.1% with added ganitumab; these estimates are not five-year overall survival.

evidence.snippet: Fracture occurred in 14 (15%) of 93 patients with long-bone ESFT, most commonly in the femur.
evidence.explanation: Retrospective long-bone cohort supports the complication, with restricted anatomy and historical treatment.

evidence.snippet: Nine (64%) of the 14 fractures occurred after the start of radiotherapy, and three of these were associated with either local recurrence or second malignancy.
evidence.explanation: Distinguishes disease-course fractures from presentation and treatment-associated fractures.

steps/34.description: Fractures can complicate osseous Ewing sarcoma at presentation or during and after treatment. A historical long-bone cohort reported fractures in 14/93 patients across the disease course, including many after radiation; this is not a disease-wide presentation frequency.

evidence.snippet: Apart from whole chromosome arm copy-number changes, the most common somatic mutations were detected in STAG2 (17%), CDKN2A (12%), TP53 (7%), EZH2, BCOR, and ZMYM3 (2.7% each).
evidence.explanation: Establishes STAG2 as one of the most common recurrent somatic alterations in Ewing sarcoma.

evidence.snippet: Among patients with localised disease, 5-year event-free survival was 54% (95% CI 34-70%) and 75% (95% CI 63-84%) for patients with STAG2 loss vs. expression (P = 0.0034).
evidence.explanation: Supports the adverse clinical association of STAG2 protein loss in localized Ewing sarcoma.

evidence.snippet: occurs by point mutation, rearrangement, and likely nongenetic mechanisms; and is associated with disease dissemination
evidence.explanation: Establishes that STAG2 inactivation is not exclusively mutational, which is what reconciles the sequencing-based frequency recorded here with the higher immunohistochemical protein-loss rate recorded beside it.

genes/1.notes: STAG2 loss-of-function mutations and protein loss are overlapping but distinct secondary alterations. Mutation frequency was 17% in one whole-genome cohort; localized COG tumors showed protein loss in 29/108 by IHC. STAG2/TP53 co-mutation was associated with poor outcome. Mutual exclusivity with CDKN2A deletion was a cohort observation, not a biological impossibility of co-alteration. The two rates are not in conflict: a separate genomic study reports STAG2 inactivation occurring by rearrangement and by likely nongenetic routes as well as by point mutation, so a sequencing frequency is expected to sit below a protein-level rate and ascertaining a STAG2-defined subgroup by sequencing alone will miss cases.

evidence.snippet: In an expanded cohort of 299 patients with clinical data, we discovered that STAG2 and TP53 mutations are often concurrent and are associated with poor outcome.
evidence.explanation: Supports TP53 mutation as part of the high-risk STAG2/TP53 co-altered Ewing sarcoma subset.

genes/2.notes: TP53 is recurrently mutated in a minority of Ewing sarcomas and co-occurs with STAG2 mutation in an aggressive secondary-genetic subset.

evidence.snippet: Strikingly, STAG2 mutations and CDKN2A deletions were mutually exclusive, as confirmed in Ewing sarcoma cell lines.
evidence.explanation: Supports CDKN2A deletion as a recurrent secondary alteration distinct from STAG2-mutant Ewing sarcoma.

genes/3.notes: CDKN2A deletion is a recurrent secondary alteration. Its reported mutual exclusivity with STAG2 mutation concerns copy-number loss in particular cohorts; absence of CDKN2A point mutations in an unarchived portal analysis does not independently verify that relationship.

evidence.snippet: For localized Ewing sarcoma, chemotherapy administered every 2 weeks is more effective than chemotherapy administered every 3 weeks, with no increase in toxicity.
evidence.explanation: The randomized COG study supports interval compression; the conclusion applies to its localized-disease population.

evidence.snippet: Dose-intensive chemotherapy with vincristine, doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide, ifosfamide, and etoposide is more effective, less toxic, and shorter in duration
evidence.explanation: EE2012 randomized evidence supports the VDC/IE approach over VIDE induction. The protocol also admitted Ewing-like sarcomas, a scope consideration when applying the result to modern molecular entities.

treatments/0.description: Interval-compressed vincristine, doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide alternating with ifosfamide and etoposide (VDC/IE), with growth-factor support and hematologic recovery criteria, is a standard systemic backbone. Randomized data support two-week over three-week scheduling in localized disease. Treatment is delivered before and after surgery and/or radiation.

evidence.snippet: surgery is the treatment of choice if tumor resection is possible with negative margins, without significant morbidity, and with a reasonable functional outcome.
evidence.explanation: Contemporary guideline supports margin-negative resection when feasible; this avoids causal superiority claims from a confounded observational treatment comparison.

treatments/1.description: Wide surgical resection with negative margins is preferred when feasible without excessive morbidity. Reconstruction may be needed for limb salvage.

evidence.snippet: Standard treatment involves multiagent induction chemotherapy followed by local treatment with surgery, definitive radiation, or a combination of surgery and radiation followed by additional chemotherapy and consolidation local treatment to metastatic sites.
evidence.explanation: Confirms the role of definitive radiation as a local treatment option in Ewing sarcoma management.

treatments/2.description: Definitive radiation is used for unresectable tumors or when surgery would cause significant morbidity. Also used post-operatively for close or positive margins.

evidence.snippet: Standard treatment involves multiagent induction chemotherapy followed by local treatment with surgery, definitive radiation, or a combination of surgery and radiation followed by additional chemotherapy and consolidation local treatment to metastatic sites.
evidence.explanation: The review describes continuation of systemic chemotherapy after local treatment.

treatments/3.description: Systemic chemotherapy continues after local control to treat occult disseminated disease. Duration and consolidation depend on protocol and risk group; a fixed 9-12-month duration is not applicable to all modern interval-compressed regimens.

evidence.snippet: In phase 2, 0 of 10 EWS subjects experienced an objective response; two experienced prolonged SD.
evidence.explanation: Clinical evidence supports feasibility but only partial therapeutic support because objective responses were not observed in the phase 2 Ewing cohort.

evidence.snippet: Two patients with Ewing sarcoma experienced a complete and a partial response for 10 and 42 cycles, respectively.
evidence.explanation: Limited activity in a later phase-I/II combination trial; this does not establish general efficacy or attribute the effect uniquely to PARP inhibition.

treatments/4.description: PARP-inhibitor combinations remain investigational in recurrent/refractory Ewing sarcoma. Talazoparib plus temozolomide produced no objective responses in ten phase-2 Ewing patients. A later pediatric olaparib-irinotecan phase-I/II study reported two Ewing responses, with a 6.3% response rate in its evaluable Ewing cohort. These limited signals do not establish routine efficacy or a validated HR-deficiency biomarker.

evidence.snippet: Here, we show that PARP inhibitor sensitivity in Ewing's sarcoma cells is not through an apparent defect in DNA repair by HR, but through hypersensitivity to trapped PARP1-DNA complexes.
evidence.explanation: Supports PARP trapping as a cellular mechanism.

treatments/4/targets/0.description: PARP inhibition interferes with PARP-dependent transcription and traps PARP-DNA complexes. Preclinical sensitivity is not equivalent to demonstrated patient benefit.

treatments/5.description: Seclidemstat (SP-2577) is an investigational LSD1-associated transcriptional modulator studied in fusion-positive sarcoma cells and trials. evidence.snippet: Seclidemstat recapitulated much of SP-2509 transcriptional activity in Ewing sarcoma.
