open_questions/1.rationale: The reported LAMB1 phenotypic spectrum spans an extraordinary range for a single gene: at the severe end, fetal hydranencephaly incompatible with life; in the middle, the cobblestone malformation with hydrocephalus that defines this entry; and at the mild end, an adult-onset leukoencephalopathy in which cortical dysgenesis was explicitly absent. The entry's genetic notes describe the truncating-versus-hypomorphic gradient as "emerging", which is the right hedge — the whole reported cohort was about eleven patients and eleven variants, far too small to establish a genotype-phenotype rule, and it does not explain how a biallelic LAMB1 genotype can spare the cortical malformation entirely. Whether the determinant is residual laminin beta-1 function, compensating laminin chains, modifier background, or developmental timing of pial basement-membrane assembly is unresolved. This is the disease-level instance of the non-one-to-one gene-to-phenotype mapping that the cortical malformation review flags as a general gap for malformations of cortical development, and it bounds what this entry may claim: the cobblestone malformation is not an obligate consequence of biallelic LAMB1 loss.

open_questions/0.rationale: The three edges out of this node -- to Abdominal pain, Constipation, and Peripheral neuropathy -- all rest on a single sentence from an ALAD-deficiency porphyria case report stating that lead produces the same biochemical and neurological picture. That sentence is an analogy, not a measurement: no source found for this entry demonstrates in lead-exposed patients that circulating ALA is what produces the colic, and the classic presentation has been attributed to precursor neurotoxicity for decades largely on the strength of the porphyria resemblance. The node is modeled with INDIRECT directness and INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES edges for this reason. Lead also acts on the same neurons by calcium mimicry, which this entry models separately, so the two routes are not distinguishable from the evidence currently cited. A study correlating ALA levels with colic severity in lead-exposed patients, independent of blood lead, would settle it.

evidence.snippet: Human disease results from inhalation of Legionella-contaminated aerosols and subsequent bacterial replication within alveolar macrophages.

evidence.snippet: To replicate intracellularly, Legionella generates a replication-permissive compartment called the Legionella-containing vacuole (LCV) through the concerted action of hundreds of Dot/Icm-translocated effector proteins.

evidence.explanation: Dedicated review of the Dot/Icm Type IVB secretion system quantifying the >300 translocated effectors and establishing their necessity for evasion of phagolysosomal degradation and for using macrophages as a replicative niche — the effector-driven basis of the Legionella-containing vacuole this node represents. steps/0.description: Legionnaires' disease results from inhalation of Legionella-contaminated aerosols followed by bacterial replication inside alveolar macrophages, where the organism establishes a replication-permissive intracellular compartment (the Legionella-containing vacuole). This obligate intracellular lifestyle is the basis for the requirement for cell-penetrant antibiotics, because beta-lactams cannot reach the cytoplasmic organism.

evidence.snippet: only macrophages from A/J mice deficient in the NAIP5 (or Birc1e) pathway of the inflammasome allow an intracellular infection. The NAIP5 pathway is involved in the recognition of flagellin.
evidence.explanation: Murine data showing that flagellin recognition through the NAIP5/NLRC4 inflammasome restricts intracellular replication, with NAIP5-deficient A/J macrophages being permissive. Evidence source is MODEL_ORGANISM as this derives from mouse macrophage models; human translational validity is inferred.

steps/1.description: Host innate immunity restricts intracellular Legionella replication through cytosolic sensing of bacterial flagellin. Flagellin is recognized by NAIP5 (BIRC1e), which nucleates the NLRC4 inflammasome, activating caspase-1 and pyroptotic death of the infected cell. In murine models this axis explains why most wild-type mouse strains are naturally non-permissive to L. pneumophila, whereas NAIP5-deficient A/J macrophages permit intracellular replication. The human relevance of this specific restriction pathway is inferred from these model-organism data.

evidence.snippet: Gastrointestinal or neurologic abnormalities were found approximately in two-thirds and relative bradycardia in 9 (52.9%).
evidence.explanation: Clinical case series documenting the extrapulmonary features (GI/neurologic abnormalities, relative bradycardia) characteristic of Legionnaires' disease. Evidence source is HUMAN_CLINICAL as this is a clinical case series.

evidence.snippet: LD was severe in 11 (64.7%) patients, which required intensive care unit follow-up.
evidence.explanation: Supports the severity of Legionnaires' disease, with most cases requiring intensive care. Evidence source is HUMAN_CLINICAL as this is a clinical case series.

steps/2.description: Legionella replication in the lung produces a severe lobar pneumonia that frequently requires intensive care. A characteristic feature is prominent extrapulmonary involvement — gastrointestinal and neurologic abnormalities and relative bradycardia — that helps distinguish Legionnaires' disease from other community-acquired pneumonias.

evidence.snippet: The therapeutic approach for atypical pneumonias is different than that for typical pneumonia.
evidence.explanation: Supports that intracellular/atypical pathogens such as Legionella require a different therapeutic approach than cell-wall-targeting beta-lactams. Evidence source is OTHER as this is a review article.

evidence.snippet: Typical bacterial pathogens classically respond to β-lactam antimicrobial therapy because they have a cell wall amenable to β-lactam disruption.
evidence.explanation: Explains why beta-lactams work against cell-walled typical pathogens but fail against the intracellular, atypical Legionella — the basis for the cell-penetrant-antibiotic requirement. Evidence source is OTHER as this is a review article.

evidence.snippet: β-lactam and aminoglycoside antibiotics are not effective in the treatment of Legionella pneumonia due to their inability to permeate the cell membrane.
evidence.explanation: Directly states that beta-lactams and aminoglycosides fail against Legionella because they cannot penetrate the host cell to reach the intracellular organism — the pharmacokinetic gating this node represents. Evidence source is OTHER as this is a review/case-report treatment summary.

steps/3.description: Because Legionella replicates inside host cells, effective treatment requires antibiotics that accumulate intracellularly — macrolides (e.g., azithromycin) and fluoroquinolones (e.g., levofloxacin) — whereas beta-lactams, which penetrate cells poorly, are ineffective. This pharmacokinetic gating, rather than a single enzyme target, governs drug selection.

evidence.snippet: The ribosome is one of the main antibiotic targets in the bacterial cell.

steps/4.description: Macrolides such as azithromycin, a first-line therapy for Legionnaires' disease, accumulate intracellularly and inhibit bacterial protein synthesis by binding the 50S subunit of the Legionella 70S ribosome — the conserved bacterial-translation target this node represents.

evidence.snippet: Quinolones dually target DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV binding to specific domains and conformations so as to block DNA strand passage catalysis and stabilize DNA-enzyme complexes that block the DNA replication apparatus and generate double breaks in DNA that underlie their bactericidal activity.
evidence.explanation: Review establishing DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV as the dual fluoroquinolone target and cleavage-complex mechanism, the levofloxacin target this node represents in Legionella therapy. Evidence source is OTHER as this is a review article.

steps/5.description: Respiratory fluoroquinolones such as levofloxacin, a first-line alternative for Legionnaires' disease, are cell-penetrant and kill intracellular Legionella by trapping the DNA gyrase/topoisomerase IV cleavage complex — the bactericidal fluoroquinolone target this node represents.

steps/2.description: NHE1 maintains intracellular pH by exchanging one intracellular proton for one extracellular sodium ion. Loss of NHE1 function leads to dysregulated intracellular pH, which is especially deleterious in the central nervous system.

steps/1.description: LIAS encodes lipoic acid synthetase, a mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster enzyme that inserts two sulfur atoms into octanoyl-GCSH to generate lipoyl-GCSH. This is the second step in the lipoylation pathway, after LIPT2-mediated octanoyl transfer and before LIPT1-mediated lipoyl relay to the E2 subunits of alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenases. LIAS deficiency, like LIPT2 deficiency, abolishes lipoylation of all downstream targets including the glycine cleavage system. This disrupts pyruvate dehydrogenase, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, branched-chain ketoacid dehydrogenase, and glycine cleavage, causing combined lactic acidosis and hyperglycinemia.

steps/2.description: LIAS deficiency reduces lipoylation of alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complexes, including pyruvate dehydrogenase, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, and branched-chain ketoacid dehydrogenase. evidence.snippet: The Phe652Leu but not the Arg486Thr protein mutant showed a weak binding to a glucosidase I-specific affinity resin, indicating that the two amino acids affect polypeptide folding and active site formation differently.

steps/1.description: Missense, frameshift and other variants on both MOGS alleles. The gene has four exons, with exon 4 encoding the 64 kDa catalytic domain, and both original disease alleles fall in that exon. Reintroducing either into wild-type glucosidase I abolished measurable activity, and the two acted differently on the protein: one retained weak affinity-resin binding and the other did not, so they disturb folding and active-site formation by different routes.

evidence.snippet: Enzymological studies on liver tissue and cultured skin fibroblasts revealed a severe glucosidase I deficiency. The residual activity was <3% of that of controls.

evidence.snippet: No significant differences in the activities of other processing enzymes, including oligosaccharyltransferase, glucosidase II, and Man(9)-mannosidase, were observed.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the defect is confined to this one enzyme, which is what lets the rest of the chain be attributed to it.

steps/2.description: Residual activity in patient tissue is under 3 percent of control in liver and fibroblasts, and under 1 percent by kinetic assay in fibroblast extracts. The loss is specific: oligosaccharyltransferase, glucosidase II and Man9-mannosidase activities are unchanged, so the block is at one enzyme rather than across the pathway.

evidence.snippet: Glucosidase I is an important enzyme in N-linked glycoprotein processing, removing specifically distal alpha-1,2-linked glucose from the Glc3Man9GlcNAc2 precursor after its en bloc transfer from dolichyl diphosphate to a nascent polypeptide chain in the endoplasmic reticulum.
evidence.explanation: Defines the reaction whose failure this node describes, and its position in the pathway.

evidence.snippet: despite the dramatically reduced glucosidase I activity, the bulk of the N-linked carbohydrate chains (>80%) in the patient's fibroblasts appeared to have been processed correctly, with only approximately 16% of the N-glycans being arrested at the Glc(3)-Man(9-7)-GlcNAc(2) stage.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies how much of the glycan pool is actually arrested, which is smaller than the near-total enzyme loss would suggest and is the reason the bypass node exists.

steps/3.description: Glucosidase I removes the distal alpha-1,2-linked glucose from the Glc3Man9GlcNAc2 precursor immediately after it is transferred en bloc from dolichyl diphosphate to the nascent chain. Without that first cut the glycan cannot enter the maturation sequence, and a fraction of N-glycans is arrested at the Glc3Man9-7GlcNAc2 stage.

steps/4.description:
Neuronal ion channels, adhesion molecules and receptors are N-glycosylated, and the standard account is that mishandling their glycans is what produces the encephalopathy. It is worth being clear that this is an inference from glycan biology plus a consistent clinical association, not a demonstrated step: no specific neuronal glycoprotein has been shown to be the one that matters, and no cited work measures a neuronal glycoprotein defect in a patient. It is recorded as HYPOTHETICAL for that reason, and the entry does not name a mechanism it cannot cite.
What is well established is the clinical output. Seizures, hypotonia and developmental delay are present in essentially every reported patient, the seizures are frequently drug-resistant, and imaging shows progressive cortical and subcortical atrophy.

evidence.snippet: By contrast, the patient's fibroblasts displayed a two- to threefold higher endo-alpha1,2-mannosidase activity, associated with an increased level of enzyme-specific mRNA-transcripts.

evidence.snippet: This points to the lack of glucosidase I activity being compensated for, to some extent, by increase in the activity of the pathway involving endo-alpha1,2-mannosidase; this would also explain the marked urinary excretion of Glc(3)-Man.

steps/5.description: Patient fibroblasts show two- to threefold higher endo-alpha-1,2-mannosidase activity with a matching rise in its transcript. That enzyme cleaves internally to the glucose block, so it clears most glycans through an alternative route and releases the Glc3Man tetrasaccharide. This single compensation explains two otherwise puzzling observations at once: why the serum transferrin pattern is normal despite a near-complete enzyme loss, and where the diagnostic urinary tetrasaccharide comes from.

evidence.snippet: This paradox phenomenon is, at least in part, because the impaired N-linked glycan processing of the patients compromises their ability to support efficient replication and cellular entry of viruses.

steps/6.description:
Enveloped viruses depend on host ER glucosidases to fold their own glycoproteins and on host glycan structures for receptor engagement, so the same block that destabilises immunoglobulin also handicaps the virus. It is the observation that made ER glucosidases a broad-spectrum antiviral target.
What this node does not claim is that patients escape infection. Recurrent infection is present in 10 of 11 reported patients; the single exception is the sibling pair in whom the reduced infectious diathesis was described, and the elder sister of a separate pair had documented cytomegalovirus infection despite CMV being an enveloped virus. The scope of the claim is reduced susceptibility to some glycosylation-dependent enveloped viruses in the patients where it was looked for, not a clinical phenotype of the disease.
The bound GO process covers the entry half of this node only. The replication half has no equally specific GO counterpart and is deliberately left unbound rather than approximated by a broader term.

steps/11.description:
Immunoglobulins carry N-glycans, and glycan structure governs their stability and circulating half-life. In MOGS-CDG the hypogammaglobulinemia is a catabolic problem rather than a production one: the mechanism identified in the two studied siblings was a shortened immunoglobulin half-life.
Serum glycomics names the specific defect behind that clearance. Patient IgG carries aberrant oligo-mannose and hybrid-type N-glycans, and its core-fucosylated complex di-antennary glycans are markedly reduced - while transferrin and alpha-1-antitrypsin move the other way, with increased sialylated species. The defect is therefore not uniform across serum glycoproteins, which is part of why transferrin-based CDG screening misses this disease.

genes/0.notes:
Encodes mannosyl-oligosaccharide glucosidase, also called ER alpha-glucosidase I or glucosidase 1. Four exons, with exon 4 encoding the 64 kDa catalytic domain.
No genotype-phenotype correlation has been established. The largest series states directly that severity varied by organ system with no definite genotype correlation, and the reported range is wide - from death at 74 days to children in their second decade. Prognostic counselling from the genotype is therefore not currently supportable.
Variants of uncertain significance are the practical difficulty. Exome sequencing turns them up faster than functional validation can resolve them, which is precisely why the urinary tetrasaccharide assay matters: it is the orthogonal test that can confirm or exclude a candidate MOGS genotype.

open_questions/0.rationale:
The human deficiency is the experiment, and it is a weaker experiment than it first appears. Patients with almost no glucosidase I activity do show impaired viral replication and entry, and one sibling pair showed limited clinical evidence of an infectious diathesis despite severe hypogammaglobulinemia. That pair is the whole of the survivability argument: across all 11 reported patients, recurrent infection is present in 10, and a patient from another pair had cytomegalovirus infection despite CMV being enveloped. So the target may well be effective; whether inhibiting it is survivable rests on two children, not on the disease. What the argument also does not establish is a therapeutic window. These patients also have a severe neurological and dysmorphic phenotype from lifelong constitutive loss, and nothing in the human data separates which of those consequences would follow acute pharmacological inhibition in an adult. The proposal is recorded as emerging on that basis.
There is also a direct negative result, from the same group that made the original observation. Testing the FDA-approved alpha-glucosidase inhibitor miglustat against SARS-CoV-2 in vitro, they found the expected structural change in the spike and ACE2 glycans without the functional consequence: miglustat did not reproduce the resistance the human deficiency shows, and they say so. That does not refute the mechanism in the constitutive human deficiency, where the block is near-total and lifelong, but it is a concrete demonstration that partial pharmacological inhibition is not the same intervention, and it belongs beside the proposal rather than in a citation nobody reads.

open_questions/1.rationale: Severity spans death at 74 days to survival into the second decade, and the largest series found no genotype correlation. The bypass is a candidate modifier that has never been tested as one: it was measured in a single patient's fibroblasts, and if its magnitude varies between individuals it would predict severity where the genotype does not. Measuring endo-alpha-1,2-mannosidase activity alongside urinary Glc3Man across the known cohort would settle it, and the samples to do that largely exist.

treatments/0.description: Anti-seizure medications are the baseline pharmacologic treatment for MTLE-HS; persistent seizures despite appropriate medication define the drug-resistant population considered for resective or ablative interventions.

evidence.snippet: We found that 73.6% of the patients were free from disabling seizures (Engel Class I), maintained over time in 65% of patients followed up to 23 years after surgery.
evidence.explanation: Supports temporal lobectomy as an effective long-term treatment for drug-resistant TLE associated with hippocampal sclerosis.

treatments/1.description: In drug-resistant MTLE-HS, temporal lobectomy provides durable seizure control for many patients and remains a key treatment strategy.

evidence.snippet: ImportanceLaser interstitial thermal therapy (LITT) is a surgical tool used to ablate epileptic foci and brain tumors.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports LITT as an ablative surgical tool for epileptic foci.

evidence.snippet: These findings indicate that LITT may be considered as a treatment option for drug-resistant MTLE.
evidence.explanation: The MTLE cohort study explicitly supports considering LITT for drug-resistant MTLE.

treatments/2.description: Laser interstitial thermal therapy is a minimally invasive ablative option for selected patients with drug-resistant mesial temporal lobe epilepsy, including MTLE-HS, when the epileptogenic focus is anatomically targetable.

evidence.snippet: Hippocampal T2 hyperintensity following febrile status epilepticus predicted hippocampal sclerosis and significant likelihood of mesial temporal lobe epilepsy.
evidence.explanation: Prospective FEBSTAT imaging supports an initial-precipitating-injury (lesion-first) pathway in which acute hippocampal injury precedes later sclerosis and MTLE.

evidence.snippet: Several etiologies may precede HS, but there is little overview in the literature about these etiologies.
evidence.explanation: Documents that multiple distinct etiologies can precede hippocampal sclerosis, keeping the cause-versus-consequence question genuinely open rather than settled.

open_questions/0.rationale: The causal direction between hippocampal sclerosis and seizures is a long-standing, unresolved chicken-or-egg question. Prospective imaging after febrile status epilepticus shows that an initial precipitating injury can predict later hippocampal sclerosis and MTLE, favoring a lesion-first model; yet the etiology of MTLE-HS is heterogeneous, with multiple risk factors that may precede HS, and seizure-driven progressive injury remains a competing account. Because dismech models the sclerotic hippocampus as the epileptogenic focus, whether that lesion is upstream cause, downstream consequence, or a self-reinforcing loop directly affects how the causal edges out of this node should be interpreted.

evidence.snippet: The mechanisms underlying TLE-HS development remain unclear, but the reactive transcriptomic changes in glial cells and neurons of the hippocampus post-epileptogenesis may provide insights.
evidence.explanation: Explicitly states that TLE-HS mechanisms are unclear and frames reactive glial and neuronal changes as candidate, not yet causally established, contributors to epileptogenesis.

open_questions/1.rationale: The mechanisms converting an injured hippocampus into a chronically epileptic network remain unresolved. Transcriptomic profiling of the epileptic hippocampus reveals many reactive changes in glia and neurons, but whether inflammatory activation and synaptic remodeling drive epileptogenesis or merely accompany it is unknown. Separating drivers from bystanders is prerequisite to any disease-modifying (antiepileptogenic) intervention and to weighting the causal edge from the sclerotic focus to network reorganization.

evidence.snippet: kainic acid (KA) was stereotactically injected into the hippocampal CA1 region of mice, followed by a 7-day postinjection period.
evidence.explanation: Describes the intracerebral kainate injection paradigm whose short time-course and induction route differ from the human febrile-SE etiology and years-long latent period, framing the translational-fidelity question.

evidence.snippet: A notable pathological change related to TLE is hippocampal sclerosis (HS), which is characterized by neuronal loss, gliosis, and an increased neuron fibre density.
evidence.explanation: Confirms the rodent model reproduces HS-like neuronal loss and gliosis, establishing that model evidence exists while its match to the human sclerosis pattern and laterality remains the open question.

open_questions/2.rationale: Rodent chemoconvulsant models reproduce HS-like neuronal loss and gliosis and generate spontaneous seizures, and are the workhorse for mechanistic and antiepileptogenesis studies. However, their fidelity to human MTLE-HS is debated: the human latent period spans years rather than days to weeks, the common human antecedent of febrile status epilepticus is not modeled by direct intracerebral excitotoxin injection, and the acute, bilateral, and often severe sclerosis induced in rodents may not match the typically unilateral, subfield-specific human sclerosis pattern. This is a model-evidence-exists-but-human-validity-uncertain gap rather than a missing assertion.

evidence.snippet: He presented with severe cardiac failure in association with a viral illness at 15 months and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy was diagnosed.
evidence.explanation: The clearest instance: cardiac failure presenting during a viral illness.

evidence.snippet: We describe a case of a child manifested as regression of mental and motor development, aggravated obviously after suffering infection
evidence.explanation: A second patient deteriorating after infection. INDIRECT because this source says "infection" without specifying a virus, while the bound ECTO term is viral - the generic exposure class is used because the one source that names the agent names a virus.

evidence.snippet: Functional studies demonstrated a severe reduction in NDUFAF1 protein in Western blots of patient fibroblasts and accumulation of abnormal complex I assembly intermediates on Blue Native polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis
evidence.explanation: Establishes loss of function at the protein level, and in the same sentence the assembly-intermediate accumulation that the next two nodes model.

evidence.snippet: These changes were absent in 240 ethnically matched control alleles
evidence.explanation: The control-allele screen, which is what makes the variants candidate causal rather than merely present.

steps/2.description: Biallelic NDUFAF1 variants reduce the amount of functional CIA30 protein. In the 2011 case the reduction was demonstrated at the protein level rather than inferred from the genotype.

evidence.snippet: The mitochondrial complex I intermediate assembly (MCIA) complex, containing assembly factors NDUFAF1, ECSIT, ACAD9, and TMEM126B, is required for building the intermediate ND2-module
evidence.explanation: Names NDUFAF1 as an MCIA component and names what the complex builds, which is what makes the lesion specific to the ND2 module rather than to assembly in general.

steps/3.description: NDUFAF1 does not work alone. It is one of four core components of the mitochondrial complex I intermediate assembly (MCIA) complex, with ECSIT, ACAD9 and TMEM126B, and that complex builds the ND2 module of complex I. Knocking out any one component is enough to impair complex I assembly, which is why an assembly-factor gene behaves like a structural one clinically.

evidence.snippet: the human complex I assembly factor CIA30 (complex I intermediate associated protein) associates with newly translated mtDNA-encoded complex I subunits at early stages in their assembly before dissociating at a later stage
evidence.explanation: Places the lesion at the early stage and describes the transient association that the `direct_intermediate_binding` hypothesis rests on.

evidence.snippet: Complex I assembly in patient cells was defective at early stages with subunits being degraded
evidence.explanation: The same early-stage defect observed in patient cells rather than in a knockdown.

evidence.snippet: NDUFAF1 is associated to two complexes of 600 and 700 kDa in size
evidence.explanation: INDIRECT because it locates NDUFAF1 on intermediate-sized complexes without itself showing that losing it blocks assembly. Cited because those sizes are what the direct-versus-indirect controversy is argued over: the 500-850 kDa range in the dissenting paper, and the ~400 kDa stalled complex seen in the index patient.

steps/4.description: CIA30 acts at the early stage of assembly, associating with newly translated mtDNA-encoded subunits and dissociating later. Without it that early step does not complete, and the intermediate that fails to form is the ND2 module.

evidence.snippet: Functional studies demonstrated a severe reduction in NDUFAF1 protein in Western blots of patient fibroblasts and accumulation of abnormal complex I assembly intermediates on Blue Native polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis
evidence.explanation: Direct visualisation of the accumulated intermediates in an NDUFAF1 patient, which is what puts this disease in the class the metabolic arm below applies to.

evidence.snippet: in patient 1 it appeared to stall in an ∼400 kDa complex
evidence.explanation: The index patient's stalled intermediate, with a size. Independent of the 2011 patient's BN-PAGE finding above, and in a different laboratory.

steps/5.description: Abnormal complex I assembly intermediates build up and were visualised directly on blue native PAGE in the 2011 patient. This node matters because the intermediates are not inert debris - the metabolic arm below is driven by them rather than by the absence of the holoenzyme.

steps/6.description: Subunits that cannot be incorporated are degraded, so the steady-state pool of complex I protein falls rather than merely failing to function.

evidence.snippet: we demonstrate that reactive oxygen species overproduction by CI assembly intermediates and subsequent AMPK-dependent Pyruvate Dehydrogenase inactivation are key players of this metabolic reprogramming
evidence.explanation: Names the intermediates as the ROS source and the AMPK-PDH step as what follows. INDIRECT for the same reason as every other item from this paper: the cohort is complex I assembly defects as a class, with no NDUFAF1 line named, so applying it here rests on the class-membership step.

steps/7.description: The stalled intermediates overproduce reactive oxygen species. This is the step that makes an assembly defect metabolically different from a functional one, and it is attributed to the intermediates rather than to the missing holoenzyme.

evidence.snippet: we demonstrate that reactive oxygen species overproduction by CI assembly intermediates and subsequent AMPK-dependent Pyruvate Dehydrogenase inactivation are key players of this metabolic reprogramming
evidence.explanation: The PDH inactivation step, named as AMPK-dependent and downstream of the ROS. INDIRECT for the class-membership reason given on the node above.

steps/8.description: Pyruvate dehydrogenase is inactivated downstream of AMPK, closing the route from pyruvate into the TCA cycle and committing pyruvate to lactate instead.

evidence.snippet: we identified a CIA30-deficient patient who presented with cardioencephalomyopathy and reduced levels and activity of complex I
evidence.explanation: Both halves of the deficiency - reduced levels and reduced activity - in the index patient, alongside the clinical syndrome.

evidence.snippet: enzymatic analysis of patient 1 lymphoblasts showed a complex I deficiency of 36% residual activity relative to the marker enzymes citrate synthase or complex II
evidence.explanation: Puts a number on the residual activity in the index patient: 36% of the marker-enzyme reference. The deficiency is partial, not absolute, which the same paper offers as the reason this patient's course was comparatively mild.

steps/9.description: Reduced amount and activity of complex I, the entry point of the respiratory chain. NADH oxidation and the proton pumping coupled to it both fall.

evidence.snippet: a complex I deficiency does not necessarily lead to a glycolytic switch, i.e. the so-called Warburg effect, but that this particular metabolic adaptation is a feature of CI assembly defect
evidence.explanation: INDIRECT because the cohort is complex I assembly defects as a class rather than NDUFAF1 patients specifically. It applies here because the 2011 NDUFAF1 patient's assembly intermediates were directly demonstrated, which is the class membership the sentence turns on.

steps/10.description: A Warburg-like reliance on glycolysis. The finding that gives this node its place in the chain is a negative one: complex I deficiency does not produce this switch in general, only assembly defects do, which is the class NDUFAF1 disease belongs to.

steps/11.description: Cardiac muscle depends heavily on oxidative ATP and has little capacity to substitute glycolysis for it. Like the neural node, this is an inferred bridge: no cached source measures cardiac bioenergetics in an NDUFAF1 patient. It deliberately does not claim the heart declares itself first, because the leukodystrophy case is a counterexample this entry carries.

evidence.snippet: This is the first report that NDUFAF1 mutations cause leukodystrophy
evidence.explanation: Establishes that NDUFAF1 loss can produce a primarily white-matter disease, which is what this node exists to carry.

steps/12.description: The neurological arm, and the one the third case is made of. This node is an inferred bridge rather than an observation: no cached source measures bioenergetics in neural tissue from any NDUFAF1 patient, and it exists to carry the neurological phenotypes the cardiac arm cannot. It is kept separate from the cardiac node because the published cases separate - three have cardiac disease and one does not.

evidence.snippet: Sequence analysis of NDUFAF1 revealed compound heterozygous missense mutations (c.631C>T;p.Arg211Cys and c.733G>A;p.Gly245Arg) in one patient with fatal infantile HCM
evidence.explanation: Ties the genotype to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in the second reported case.

evidence.snippet: We here describe a new case of apparently isolated HCM due to mitochondrial assembly factor gene NDUFAF1 biallelic variants
evidence.explanation: An independent case, and the one where the cardiomyopathy was the whole of the presentation rather than part of a multisystem picture.

evidence.snippet: He presented with severe cardiac failure in association with a viral illness at 15 months and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy was diagnosed.
evidence.explanation: The index case's cardiomyopathy, which is the third of the three. Note the viral illness as the precipitant of the decompensation that revealed it.

steps/13.description: Reported in three of the four published cases; the leukodystrophy case reports none. In the 2025 patient the cardiomyopathy prompted the genetic workup. In the 2011 patient it did not: that workup began from a biochemical complex I deficiency in a 30-patient cohort, and the cardiomyopathy was the phenotype of the one patient in it who turned out to carry NDUFAF1 variants.

evidence.snippet: we identified a CIA30-deficient patient who presented with cardioencephalomyopathy and reduced levels and activity of complex I
evidence.explanation: Cardioencephalomyopathy names both the cardiac and the encephalopathic component in the index patient.

evidence.snippet: We here describe a new case of apparently isolated HCM due to mitochondrial assembly factor gene NDUFAF1 biallelic variants
evidence.explanation: NO_EVIDENCE rather than REFUTE. The 2007 case establishes that encephalopathy occurs in this disease and this paper does not contradict that; it reports a patient in whom the presentation was cardiac alone. The point it makes is about frequency, which this node does not claim. Note the authors' own hedge, "apparently" isolated.

steps/14.description: Present in the index case as the encephalo- half of cardioencephalomyopathy. The 2025 case is reported as "apparently isolated" cardiomyopathy, which is the authors' hedge and not a documented absence. This entry records encephalopathy as a feature of the disease's range rather than of every patient.

evidence.snippet: Patient 1 was first investigated at 11 months for failure to thrive.
evidence.explanation: The index patient's presenting complaint, four months before the cardiomyopathy.

steps/15.description: The first thing wrong in the index case, and it preceded the cardiac diagnosis.

edges/1.description: NDUFAF1 is one of the four core components of the MCIA complex, so losing it is a lesion in that complex.

evidence.snippet: Modulating the intramitochondrial amount of NDUFAF1 by knocking down its expression using RNA interference leads to a reduced amount and activity of complex I
evidence.explanation: The knockdown experiment, which is the edge claim rather than either node: reducing NDUFAF1 is what reduces complex I.

edges/2.description: Losing the assembly factor blocks the step it chaperones. This edge is the one the direct-binding account owns; the alternative hypothesis disputes the mechanism of this step, not that the step fails.

evidence.snippet: Cell knockout studies reveal that while each MCIA component is critical for complex I assembly, a hierarchy of stability exists centered on ACAD9
evidence.explanation: Establishes that losing any single MCIA component impairs complex I assembly, which is this edge. The ACAD9-centred stability hierarchy is noted but not modelled here.

edges/3.description: A defective MCIA complex cannot build the intermediate it exists to build.

edges/4.description: A blocked assembly line leaves partly built product on it.

evidence.snippet: Complex I assembly in patient cells was defective at early stages with subunits being degraded
evidence.explanation: Names the degradation as the consequence of the early-stage defect, which is this edge rather than either node alone.

edges/5.description: Subunits that never reach a stable complex are turned over.

edges/6.description: The intermediates are themselves the ROS source.

edges/7.description: Loss of subunit protein is loss of holoenzyme.

edges/8.description: The myocardium is among the tissues least able to tolerate a fall in oxidative ATP supply.

edges/9.description: The same energetic failure in neural tissue, which is what the leukodystrophy case presented with.

edges/14.description: The retina is among the most oxidative tissues in the body, which is the usual reason mitochondrial disease reaches it, but no cached source establishes that route here.

edges/15.description: Reported in the leukodystrophy case and explicitly not accounted for by that diagnosis, so the intermediates really are unknown rather than merely unstated.

edges/16.description: Blocked NADH reoxidation and the glycolytic shift together raise lactate.

edges/17.description: The mechanism the same sentence specifies.

edges/18.description: With pyruvate barred from the TCA cycle, ATP supply falls back on glycolysis.

edges/20.description: Energetic failure in the myocardium drives the hypertrophic remodelling reported in three of the four published cases.

edges/21.description: A conduction abnormality rather than a hypertrophic one, reported in the index patient alone and years after the cardiomyopathy. Nothing cached links it mechanistically to the energetic defect.

edges/22.description: The neurological arm of the index patient's cardioencephalomyopathy. The intermediates are unknown, and what determines neurological involvement across the four cases is not explained.

edges/24.description: Kept on this node rather than under Leukodystrophy because a peripheral neuropathy is a Schwann-cell and axonal problem rather than a central white-matter one, even though the source lists it among the findings pointing to that diagnosis.

edges/29.description: The source presents the regression as the clinical course of the white-matter disease rather than as a parallel output of the metabolic lesion.

edges/30.description: An upper-motor-neuron sign, and one of the findings the source says pointed to the leukodystrophy diagnosis.

evidence.snippet: He presented with severe cardiac failure in association with a viral illness at 15 months and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy was diagnosed.
evidence.explanation: The index patient's decompensation, explicitly in association with a viral illness.

edges/31.description: Infection raises energy demand and catabolic load on a system with no oxidative reserve. The mechanism is not measured in any NDUFAF1 patient, so the link is recorded as exacerbating an existing deficiency rather than as a described pathway.

evidence.snippet: NDUFAF1 is a mitochondrial protein that is involved in the complex I assembly process
evidence.explanation: The founding characterisation of the gene product as a mitochondrial complex I assembly protein.

evidence.snippet: Genetic analysis revealed the patient had mutations in both alleles of the NDUFAF1 gene that encodes CIA30
evidence.explanation: The gene-disease link in the index patient.

genes/0.notes: NDUFAF1 encodes CIA30, the human homologue of the Neurospora crassa complex I chaperone. MONDO records NDUFAF1 as the causal gene for MONDO:0032617 (RO:0004003 HGNC:18828), checked against the local build rather than assumed.

hypotheses/0.description: CIA30 associates with newly translated mtDNA-encoded subunits at early assembly and dissociates later, so its role is a direct chaperoning of the intermediate. This is the account the founding papers give and the one the entry's main chain follows.

hypotheses/1.description: A survey of complex I-deficient patient cells found NDUFAF1 still bound to the 500-850 kDa subcomplexes in a patient whose assembly intermediates were absent altogether, and that its association did not track the nature or severity of the assembly defect. Those authors concluded the involvement could be indirect. Nothing in the cached literature resolves this against the direct account.

evidence.snippet: the human complex I assembly factor CIA30 (complex I intermediate associated protein) associates with newly translated mtDNA-encoded complex I subunits at early stages in their assembly before dissociating at a later stage
evidence.explanation: The direct-association account.

evidence.snippet: suggest that the involvement of NDUFAF1 in the assembly process could be indirect rather than direct via the binding to assembly intermediates
evidence.explanation: The authors' own conclusion against the direct account, from the patient-cell survey.

open_questions/0.rationale: The founding EMBO J paper reports CIA30 associating with newly translated mtDNA-encoded subunits at early assembly and dissociating later, which reads as direct chaperoning and is what this entry's main chain assumes. A survey of complex I-deficient patient cells published the same year reaches the opposite reading: NDUFAF1's association with the 500-850 kDa subcomplexes did not track the nature or severity of the assembly defect, and persisted even in a patient whose assembly intermediates were absent because of an unrelated translation-elongation defect. If NDUFAF1 stays bound when there is nothing to bind, the association is not obviously the mechanism. This matters for the entry because the ROS arm attributes the metabolic phenotype to the intermediates themselves, and that arm is unaffected either way - but the description of what NDUFAF1 does at the assembly step is not settled by anything cached here.

evidence.snippet: Here, we describe rare biallelic variants in NDUFB8 encoding a complex I accessory subunit revealed by whole-exome sequencing in two individuals from two families.
evidence.explanation: The variants and how they were found.

evidence.snippet: Patient 2 carried a p.Tyr62His mutation and a loss-of-function deletion Glu63Aspfs*35 (c. 189delA).
evidence.explanation: The second patient's two alleles, named.

evidence.snippet: This curation included five unique variants (four missense, one frameshift) identified in three unrelated cases from two publications (PMIDs: 29429571, 30770271).
evidence.explanation: The full allelic tally across the literature, and the count of unrelated cases the entity rests on. Graded OTHER because a curation narrative is an expert synthesis.

evidence.snippet: The mechanism of disease is loss of function.
evidence.explanation: The expert panel's reading of the mechanism, which is what this node's functional_impact_category records.

steps/1.description: Two damaged copies of NDUFB8, in a compound-heterozygous configuration in both 2018 patients. Patient 1 carried p.Pro76Gln in trans with p.Cys144Trp; Pro76 lies in a highly conserved matrix-side region above the ND5 lateral helix and close to ND4, while Cys144 sits in the membrane domain and appears to form a disulfide with Cys279 of ND5. Patient 2 carried p.Tyr62His, at a residue whose hydroxyl hydrogen-bonds to Asp74 of NDUFB8 and which lies 4 to 5 angstrom from Pro76 in the same conserved patch, in trans with the frameshift p.Glu63Aspfs*35 (c.189delA). ClinGen's 2024 recuration counted five unique variants across the three published cases and read the mechanism as loss of function.

evidence.snippet: Surprisingly, it was discovered that the p.Cys144Trp mutation generated a new exonic splicing silencer (ESS).
evidence.explanation: The mechanism of the allele, stated as a finding rather than a prediction.

evidence.snippet: Nevertheless, 14% of total cDNA from Patient 1 contained the p.Cys144Trp missense mutation, indicating that while skipping exon 4 is favored, normal splicing also occurs at a lower frequency.
evidence.explanation: The quantitative limit on the skipping claim, and the reason this node describes a mixture rather than a null allele.

steps/2.description: The c.432C>G (p.Cys144Trp) allele behaves mostly as a splicing variant rather than a missense one. It creates a new exonic splicing silencer, and Sanger sequencing of patient cDNA showed skipping of exon 4, which encodes Met105 to Val156 - the segment carrying the transmembrane helix. Skipping is favoured but not complete: about 14 percent of total cDNA still carried the missense sequence, so the allele produces a mixture of a large in-frame-disrupting deletion product and a low level of full-length mutant protein. This is the one place in the entity where the molecular consequence of an allele is not what its protein-level nomenclature suggests.

evidence.snippet: NDUFB8 clamps the lateral helix of core subunit ND5.
evidence.explanation: The single structural fact that best explains why loss of a small accessory subunit is an assembly defect. Graded OTHER because this is a review's structural synthesis rather than an experiment.

evidence.snippet: On the matrix side NDUFB8 mainly contacts core subunit ND5 and NDUFB4, but it also contacts core subunit ND4 and NDUFB9.
evidence.explanation: The contact map that defines which parts of the enzyme lose a partner when NDUFB8 goes. Graded OTHER for the same reason.

evidence.snippet: The NDUFB8 subunit is initially synthesized with 186 residues and a mass of about 22 kDa, but the first 28 residues serve as a transit peptide and are cleaved off during processing.
evidence.explanation: The protein's size and its mitochondrial targeting, which is the context for the frameshift and exon-skipping alleles above.

steps/3.description: NDUFB8 sits at the distal, proton-pumping end of complex I in the ND5 module, spanning the inner membrane once with its N-terminus in the matrix and its C-terminus in the intermembrane space. Its defining structural role is to clamp the long lateral helix of the core subunit ND5; on the matrix side it also contacts ND5 and NDUFB4 and, more weakly, ND4 and NDUFB9, and on the intermembrane-space side NDUFB7 and NDUFB10. With NDUFB3 and NDUFB6 it encloses the distal end of the enzyme. Losing it therefore removes a structural brace at a module interface rather than a catalytic component.

evidence.snippet: In a knockout strain of cultured human cells, the loss of NDUFB8 resulted in no assembly of complex I
evidence.explanation: The direct demonstration that NDUFB8 is required for assembly, in a cell line rather than in a patient.

evidence.snippet: We show that 25 subunits are strictly required for assembly of a functional complex and 1 subunit is essential for cell viability.
evidence.explanation: The systematic knockout survey that the NDUFB8 result above comes from, giving the denominator against which "strictly required" is a meaningful statement.

evidence.snippet: Quantitative proteomic analysis of cell lines revealed that loss of each subunit affects the stability of other subunits residing in the same structural module.
evidence.explanation: The general module-destabilisation rule. INDIRECT because it is stated across all accessory subunits rather than measured for NDUFB8 specifically; no complexome or proteomic profile of an NDUFB8 patient has been published.

steps/4.description:
Without NDUFB8 the enzyme does not assemble. In a human knockout cell line the loss of NDUFB8 leaves no assembled complex I detectable, and NDUFB8 falls among the 25 accessory subunits that a systematic gene-editing survey found to be strictly required for a functional complex. The general rule established by that survey - that losing one subunit destabilises the other subunits of its own structural module - is the mechanism by which a single missing brace propagates into a whole-enzyme failure.
The knockout evidence is a complete null; the patient alleles are not, which is why this node is written as a failure of assembly rather than an absence of the enzyme, and why patients retain measurable residual activity.

evidence.snippet: Biochemical analyses showed an isolated decrease in complex I enzymatic activity in muscle and fibroblasts.
evidence.explanation: The defining biochemical finding, in two tissues, and its isolation to complex I.

evidence.snippet: Complementation studies by expression of wild-type NDUFB8 in cells from affected individuals restored mitochondrial function, confirming NDUFB8 variants as the cause of complex I deficiency.
evidence.explanation: The rescue that ties the enzyme defect back to the genotype in the patients' own cells.

steps/5.description: The measurable consequence in patient tissue: a decrease in complex I enzymatic activity in both muscle and fibroblasts, with the other respiratory chain complexes spared. The deficiency is isolated, which is what places the entity among the complex I deficiencies rather than among the combined oxidative phosphorylation defects. Residual activity figures for the individual patients are not given in the sources available here.

evidence.snippet: Complex I exists in supercomplex forms with respiratory chain complexes III and IV, which are together required for the generation of a transmembrane proton gradient used for the synthesis of ATP.
evidence.explanation: The link from complex I function to the proton gradient and ATP synthesis. INDIRECT because it states the general bioenergetics rather than a measurement in an NDUFB8 patient.

evidence.snippet: Complementation studies by expression of wild-type NDUFB8 in cells from affected individuals restored mitochondrial function, confirming NDUFB8 variants as the cause of complex I deficiency.
evidence.explanation: "Restored mitochondrial function" is the closest the source comes to a functional bioenergetic readout in these patients. INDIRECT because the phrase does not name the quantity measured.

steps/6.description:
Complex I is the entry point for NADH-derived electrons into the respiratory chain and pumps four protons per NADH oxidised, so a complex I defect cuts both the electron flux into the chain and the proton-motive force that drives ATP synthesis. Cells retain succinate-driven, complex II-dependent respiration, which is why the defect is survivable at all and why severity tracks residual complex I activity and tissue energy demand rather than being uniformly lethal.
This node is a mechanistic inference from the measured enzyme deficiency above rather than a separately measured quantity in these patients: no respirometry or ATP-synthesis measurement from an NDUFB8 patient is reported in the sources cited here, beyond the statement that complementation restored mitochondrial function.

evidence.snippet: Neuroimaging disclosed progressive changes in the basal ganglia and either brain stem or internal capsule.
evidence.explanation: The regional distribution of the lesions, and that they progress.

evidence.snippet: Similar to patients with Leigh syndrome, both patients showed symmetrical basal ganglia and capsula interna lesions.
evidence.explanation: The symmetry of the lesions, which is what makes the pattern Leigh-like rather than simply ischaemic or inflammatory.

steps/7.description:
Deep grey matter and brainstem nuclei have among the highest oxidative demands in the body, and in complex I deficiency they are where the lesions appear. Both 2018 patients showed progressive symmetrical basal ganglia change on neuroimaging, extending to the brain stem in one and to the internal capsule in the other - the Leigh-like pattern the paper's title names. The third reported patient instead had cavitating leukoencephalopathy, so the imaging phenotype of the entity is not confined to a single pattern.
Why these particular structures fail while others do not is the standing unanswered question of Leigh-syndrome biology generally, and nothing in the NDUFB8 literature addresses it; the node asserts the regional vulnerability, not an explanation for it.

evidence.snippet: Hypertrophy of the left cardiac ventricle was observed in Patient 1, and he died at 15 months of age. Patient 2 was still alive at six years of age.
evidence.explanation: The cardiac finding attributed to a named patient, together with the divergent outcomes that make the attribution matter.

steps/8.description: Cardiac muscle is oxidative and post-mitotic, and hypertrophy is a recognised cardiac response to a mitochondrial energy deficit. Cardiac hypertrophy is listed among the encephalo(cardio)myopathic features of the entity, and left ventricular hypertrophy was recorded specifically in the patient who died at 15 months. The parenthetical in the source paper's own phrasing signals that the cardiac component is not universal, and the phenotype below is graded accordingly.

evidence.snippet: Both presented with a progressive course of disease with encephalo(cardio)myopathic features including muscular hypotonia, cardiac hypertrophy, respiratory failure, failure to thrive, and developmental delay.
evidence.explanation: The muscular and respiratory features, and that the course is progressive.

steps/9.description: Skeletal muscle carries the highest complex I load of any tissue at exercise and is where the enzyme deficiency was measured. Muscular hypotonia was present in both 2018 patients from the earliest months, and respiratory failure - the terminal event in most severe infantile mitochondrial disease - is listed among the features of the entity. No muscle histology, ragged-red fibre count or COX/SDH histochemistry for an NDUFB8 patient is reported in the sources cited here.

evidence.snippet: Blood lactate was elevated. Neuroimaging disclosed progressive changes in the basal ganglia and either brain stem or internal capsule.
evidence.explanation: The elevated lactate in the two index patients. INDIRECT for this node because the observation is the raised lactate itself, not the redox mechanism the node names.

steps/10.description: A complex I defect leaves NADH unoxidised, and the cytosolic NADH/NAD+ ratio is restored instead by lactate dehydrogenase reducing pyruvate to lactate. Raised blood lactate is the routine clinical signature of that shift and was present in both 2018 patients. The step is standard mitochondrial-disease biochemistry rather than something demonstrated in these patients, and is curated as such.

evidence.snippet: Biochemical analyses showed an isolated decrease in complex I enzymatic activity in muscle and fibroblasts.

evidence.snippet: Both presented with a progressive course of disease with encephalo(cardio)myopathic features including muscular hypotonia, cardiac hypertrophy, respiratory failure, failure to thrive, and developmental delay.
evidence.explanation: Respiratory failure named among the features of the two index patients.

evidence.explanation: The finding attributed to one named patient of the two, which is what sets the frequency band.

Cardiac hypertrophy appears in the entity's feature list in a parenthetical - "encephalo(cardio)myopathic" - which is the source's own signal that the cardiac component is not present in every patient.

evidence.explanation: The only report of seizures in this entity. Graded OTHER because a curation narrative is an expert synthesis rather than a study.

evidence.snippet: Pathogenic or likely pathogenic mutations in eight genes were identified in 31 individuals (83.78%): IBA57 (17/37), NDUFS1 (5/37), NDUFV1 (2/37), NDUFV2 (3/37), NDUFAF5 (1/37), LYRM7 (1/37), NDUFB8 (1/37), and GLRX5 (1/37).
evidence.explanation: The one NDUFB8 patient, with the cohort denominator. Quoted as the flattened gene list because that is where the count sits in the source.

evidence.snippet: Mutations in NDUFV2, NDUFAF5, NDUFB8, or GLRX5 were first found to be related to cavitating leukoencephalopathies.
evidence.explanation: That this imaging phenotype was new for NDUFB8 at the time of that report.

evidence.snippet: Two cases had LSS and the third had cavitating leukoencephalopathy.
evidence.explanation: The expert panel's split of the three published cases between the two imaging phenotypes. Graded OTHER because a curation narrative is an expert synthesis.

steps/20.description: The third published patient, ascertained in a Chinese cohort of 37 children with cavitating leukoencephalopathies, was the single NDUFB8 case in that series. Cavitating leukoencephalopathy had not previously been associated with NDUFB8, and the finding broadens the entity's imaging phenotype beyond the Leigh-like basal ganglia pattern of the two index patients.

edges/3.description: Applies to the p.Cys144Trp allele of Patient 1 only, and is the reason that allele is not simply a missense change.

edges/14.description: Growth failure in a mitochondrial disease is conventionally read as the systemic cost of a whole-body energy deficit. The edge is marked INDIRECT because no source cited here demonstrates that pathway in an NDUFB8 patient; what is reported is the co-occurrence of failure to thrive with the enzyme defect.

evidence.snippet: Hereby we establish NDUFB8 as a relevant gene in childhood-onset mitochondrial disease.
evidence.explanation: The gene-disease relationship as claimed by the report that established it.

evidence.snippet: Complementation studies by expression of wild-type NDUFB8 in cells from affected individuals restored mitochondrial function, confirming NDUFB8 variants as the cause of complex I deficiency.
evidence.explanation: The complementation result that converts a variant association into a causal claim.

evidence.snippet: In summary, there is moderate evidence to support the relationship between NDUFB8 and autosomal recessive NDUFB8 -related primary mitochondrial disease.
evidence.explanation: The independent strength-of-evidence judgement, which is Moderate rather than Definitive and is a fair reflection of a three-case series with strong functional data. Graded OTHER because a curation assertion is an expert judgement rather than a study.

evidence.snippet: NDUFB8 has been associated with a single disease entity to date; mitochondrial complex I deficiency, nuclear type 32 [OMIM# 618252].
evidence.explanation: The lumping decision behind this entry: NDUFB8 has one disease entity, not an allelic series, so a single standalone entry is the correct shape. Graded OTHER as above.

genes/0.notes:
NDUFB8 encodes NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase subunit B8, an accessory subunit of the distal membrane arm of complex I. Its structural position - clamping the ND5 lateral helix at the ND5-module interface - is the mechanism of this disease and is curated as its own pathophysiology node.
Two traps for anyone extending this entry from the gene rather than from the disease.
First, and by far the larger, NDUFB8 is the standard antibody target for complex I in the OXPHOS immunoblot and immunofluorescence panels used across mitochondrial diagnostics and cell biology. The great majority of papers naming NDUFB8 are using reduced NDUFB8 staining as a *readout* of complex I loss caused by something else entirely - PUS1, MCAT, EARS2, NDUFA13, ERCC6, and many others. Those papers say nothing about NDUFB8 as a disease gene, and a literature search on the symbol returns them in overwhelming preponderance over the three actual patient reports.
Second, ClinGen's classification is Moderate, not Definitive, and has been recurated once - originally against Leigh syndrome spectrum in 2020, then against NDUFB8-related primary mitochondrial disease in 2024, with the Leigh cases folded into the broader entity. The two curations are the same relationship under two disease labels, not two independent lines of support.

treatments/0.description: No disease-modifying therapy exists for MC1DN32, and none has been trialled: the published literature is three case descriptions with no treatment arm. Management is the supportive care used across infantile mitochondrial disease - nutritional support for failure to thrive, respiratory support, developmental and physical therapy, and anticonvulsants where seizures occur. None of that is specific to NDUFB8, and none of it is reported for these patients in the sources cited here.

open_questions/0.rationale: The assembly claim in this entry rests on a knockout cell line, not on patient material. Sibling entities in the MC1DN series - MC1DN33 for NDUFA6, MC1DN36 for NDUFC2 - are built on complexome profiling of patient fibroblasts, which resolves exactly which subunits and subassemblies are lost and shows where biogenesis stalls. No equivalent profile has been published for an NDUFB8 patient. This matters beyond completeness: the patients are compound heterozygotes with residual activity, and one of the four alleles is a splicing variant that still yields some full-length protein, so the patient assembly defect is very unlikely to be the total failure the knockout shows. The shape of the residual assembly intermediate is what would distinguish an unstable holoenzyme from a stalled biogenesis.

open_questions/1.rationale: The two 2018 patients had markedly different outcomes - left ventricular hypertrophy and death at 15 months in one, survival to at least six years in the other - and different allele pairs. It is tempting to read the outcome difference off the genotype, and the entry deliberately does not: with one patient per genotype there is no way to separate an allele effect from a modifier, a stochastic, or an ascertainment effect, and neither source attempts the attribution. The third patient's genotype-phenotype relationship is not reported at all. Answering this needs more patients, not more analysis of these two.

evidence.snippet: Our results show that TMEM70 is involved in mitochondrial ATP synthase biogenesis in higher eukaryotes.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the molecular function that is lost.

evidence.snippet: the other two ATPAF2 and TMEM70 encode specific ancillary factors that facilitate the biogenesis of ATP synthase
evidence.explanation: Review classifying TMEM70 as a biogenesis (ancillary) factor rather than a structural subunit; graded OTHER as a synthesis of biochemical and clinical reports.

steps/1.description: TMEM70 is an ancillary factor required for the biogenesis of mitochondrial ATP synthase in higher eukaryotes. Biallelic loss-of-function variants — usually the c.317-2A>G founder splice defect — remove this biogenesis support. The causal role is proven by complementation: restoring wild-type TMEM70 to patient cells restores assembly and metabolic function of the enzyme complex.

evidence.snippet: a marked accumulation of F1 complexes indicative of impairment in ATP synthase biogenesis that was stalled at the early stage, following the formation of F1 oligomer
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates the stalled-at-F1 assembly signature and free-F1 accumulation in the constitutive Tmem70 knockout; graded MODEL_ORGANISM as a mouse finding.

steps/2.description: TMEM70 acts late in ATP synthase assembly, after the soluble F1 head has formed, so its loss stalls biogenesis at the F1 stage: the F1 oligomer is built but cannot be completed into holo-enzyme, and free F1 complexes accumulate. This is the mechanistic feature that distinguishes MC5DN2 from the ATPAF2 sibling disorder (MC5DN1), where the F1 assembly chaperone ATP12 is lost, F1 itself cannot form, and free F1 does not accumulate. Shown directly in the Tmem70-knockout mouse; human patient tissue shows the reciprocal, reduced fully assembled complex with F1 subunits still detectable.

evidence.snippet: Biochemical analysis of mitochondrial complexes showed an almost complete ATP synthase deficiency.
evidence.explanation: The defining biochemical lesion measured in patient tissue.

evidence.snippet: All these defects share a similar biochemical phenotype with pronounced decrease in the content of fully assembled and functional ATP synthase complex.
evidence.explanation: Review statement of the shared biochemical phenotype across nuclear ATP synthase defects, TMEM70 included.

steps/3.description: The content of fully assembled, functional complex V falls to a fraction of normal — in the severest biopsies an almost complete deficiency — while respiratory chain complexes I-IV are spared, the biochemical signature that distinguishes isolated complex V deficiency from combined OXPHOS defects.

evidence.snippet: While light microscopy was unremarkable, ultrastructural investigation of muscle tissue revealed accumulation of swollen degenerated mitochondria with lipid crystalloid inclusions, cristae aggregation, and exocytosis of mitochondrial material.
evidence.explanation: The ultrastructural pathology observed in patient muscle.

steps/4.description: Muscle mitochondria in TMEM70 patients accumulate swollen, degenerated forms with lipid crystalloid inclusions, cristae aggregation and exocytosis of mitochondrial material, even when light microscopy is unremarkable — complex V deficiency degrades mitochondrial morphology, consistent with the role of ATP synthase in shaping cristae.

evidence.snippet: profound lactic acidosis (lactate 5-36 mmol/l; 92%) with hyperammonaemia (100-520 micromol/l; 86%) were present from birth
evidence.explanation: The systemic metabolic decompensation quantified in the founder cohort.

evidence.snippet: In four surviving patients, life-threatening hyperammonaemia occurred during childhood, triggered by acute gastroenteritis and prolonged fasting.
evidence.explanation: The catabolic-stress-triggered crisis pattern in survivors.

evidence.snippet: Ten patients died within the first 6 weeks of life.
evidence.explanation: The early mortality burden of the decompensated neonatal course.

steps/5.description: Failure of aerobic ATP production produces profound neonatal lactic acidosis with hyperammonaemia, and a persistent increase in 3-methylglutaconic acid excretion — the metabolic triad of the disorder. After the neonatal period, life-threatening hyperammonaemic crises recur with catabolic stress such as acute gastroenteritis and prolonged fasting. Mortality is front-loaded: ten of the 25 founder-cohort patients died within the first six weeks of life.

evidence.snippet: Severe muscular hypotonia (in 92% of newborns), apnoic spells (92%), hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCMP; 76%) and profound lactic acidosis (lactate 5-36 mmol/l; 92%) with hyperammonaemia (100-520 micromol/l; 86%) were present from birth.
evidence.explanation: 92% of newborns in the founder cohort had severe hypotonia.

steps/6.description: Severe muscular hypotonia is near-universal from birth and persists in survivors of the neonatal period.

evidence.snippet: Severe muscular hypotonia (in 92% of newborns), apnoic spells (92%), hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCMP; 76%) and profound lactic acidosis (lactate 5-36 mmol/l; 92%) with hyperammonaemia (100-520 micromol/l; 86%) were present from birth.
evidence.explanation: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in 76% of the founder cohort.

evidence.snippet: HCMP was non-progressive and even disappeared in some children.
evidence.explanation: The unusual non-progressive, sometimes regressing course.

steps/7.description: Present in three quarters of neonates; characteristically non-progressive and may regress in survivors. In a minority the cardiac presentation is instead a noncompaction cardiomyopathy (recorded as the organ impairment in the ATP-synthase-deficiency sibship of PMID:26550569), so the cardiac phenotype spans hypertrophic and noncompaction morphologies rather than being purely hypertrophic.

evidence.snippet: Most patients surviving the neonatal period had persisting muscular hypotonia and developed psychomotor delay.
evidence.explanation: The developmental outcome in neonatal-period survivors.

evidence.snippet: Complementation of the cell lines of these individuals with wild-type TMEM70 restored biogenesis and metabolic function of the enzyme complex.
evidence.explanation: Complementation shows the TMEM70 lesion is what causes the enzyme deficiency: restoring the protein restores the complex.

edges/6.description: The energy-deficient myocardium hypertrophies; the cardiomyopathy is typically non-progressive once the neonatal period is survived.

evidence.snippet: We carried out whole-genome homozygosity mapping, gene expression analysis and DNA sequencing in individuals with isolated mitochondrial ATP synthase deficiency and identified disease-causing mutations in TMEM70.
evidence.explanation: The gene-discovery study establishing TMEM70 as the cause of this disorder.

evidence.snippet: To date, at least 14 additional TMEM70 mutations have been described leading to a broad clinical spectrum such as hypospadia
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the allelic spectrum extends well beyond the founder allele, and that the wider spectrum carries additional phenotypes (the same sentence continues to name pulmonary arterial hypertension).

genes/0.notes: TMEM70 (8q21.11) encodes a 21 kD inner-mitochondrial-membrane protein of three exons acting as an ancillary factor in ATP synthase biogenesis; the precise molecular function is not fully determined. The founder splice-site variant c.317-2A>G accounts for the great majority of alleles and is strongly enriched in the Roma population, but it is not the whole spectrum: at least 14 further TMEM70 mutations are reported, and the broader allelic spectrum widens the phenotype to include hypospadias and pulmonary arterial hypertension.

evidence.snippet: In summary, TMEM70 mutations can cause distinct ultrastructural mitochondrial degeneration and almost complete deficiency of ATP synthase but are still amenable to treatment.
evidence.explanation: The authors' conclusion that the disorder is treatable at the level of crisis management.

treatments/0.description: There is no disease-modifying therapy. Management is supportive — ventilatory support, correction of acidosis and hyperammonaemia, and avoidance of catabolic stress (prolonged fasting, intercurrent illness). In one consanguineous sibship, recurrent life-threatening metabolic crises were successfully stabilised with supplementation of anaplerotic amino acids and lipids combined with symptomatic crisis treatment, the basis for describing the disorder as amenable to treatment.

evidence.snippet: the other two had recurrent life-threatening metabolic crises but were successfully managed with supplementation of anaplerotic amino acids, lipids, and symptomatic treatment during metabolic crisis
evidence.explanation: The reported stabilisation of two siblings with anaplerotic supplementation targeting the metabolic decompensation.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Anaplerotic substrates and crisis management address the metabolic decompensation rather than the enzyme defect.

evidence.snippet: such plaques may suddenly cause life-threatening coronary thrombosis presenting as an acute coronary syndrome.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that rupture of an atherosclerotic plaque precipitates coronary thrombosis presenting as acute coronary syndrome (including MI).

evidence.snippet: Most often, the culprit morphology is plaque rupture with exposure of highly thrombogenic, red cell-rich necrotic core material.
evidence.explanation: Identifies plaque rupture exposing thrombogenic necrotic-core material as the dominant culprit lesion mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Type 1 is associated with atherosclerosis, type 2 results from inadequate oxygen supply to cardiomyocytes, type 3 is defined as sudden cardiac death, while types 4 and 5 are associated with procedures such as percutaneous coronary intervention and coronary artery bypass grafting, respectively.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the universal MI classification and that type 1 (the mechanism modeled here) is the atherosclerosis-driven form.

steps/0.description: A coronary atherosclerotic plaque with a thin fibrous cap and a large necrotic core ruptures (or, less often, erodes), exposing highly thrombogenic necrotic-core material and subendothelial collagen to flowing blood. Platelet adhesion and activation with activation of the coagulation cascade form an occlusive or near-occlusive coronary thrombus that abruptly interrupts blood flow to the downstream myocardium. Systemic inflammation, including that accompanying acute respiratory infection, can destabilize vulnerable plaque and promote a procoagulant state.

evidence.snippet: Myocardial infarction is defined as sudden ischemic death of myocardial tissue.
evidence.explanation: Directly evidences that MI is ischemic death of myocardium, the core claim of this node.

evidence.snippet: Mitochondrial alterations are prominently involved in apoptosis and necrosis of cardiomyocytes in the infarcted heart.
evidence.explanation: Evidences ischemic cardiomyocyte necrosis and apoptosis in the infarcted myocardium described by this node.

steps/1.description: Sustained interruption of coronary perfusion causes regional myocardial ischemia. If flow is not restored, cardiomyocytes undergo necrosis and apoptosis, releasing cardiac troponin into the circulation (the biomarker basis of MI diagnosis). Loss of contractile myocardium reduces left ventricular systolic function and provides an arrhythmogenic substrate, and can progress to heart failure.

evidence.snippet: reperfusion salvages a significant amount of ischemic myocardium in the subepicardium while reperfusion injury contributes up to 50% of the final subendocardial infarct.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that reperfusion, while salvaging myocardium, contributes up to half of the final infarct size — the defining claim of MIRI.

evidence.snippet: Reperfusion of severely ischemic myocardium leads to sustained opening of the mitochondrial permeability transition pore (MPTP).
evidence.explanation: Evidences the central mitochondrial mechanism (sustained MPTP opening) of lethal reperfusion injury described in this node.

evidence.snippet: MIRI refers to paradoxical myocardial damage that occurs upon restoration of coronary blood flow and is driven by complex inflammatory, oxidative, and metabolic mechanisms, which can exacerbate infarct size
evidence.explanation: Defines MIRI as paradoxical reperfusion damage driven by inflammatory, oxidative, and metabolic mechanisms that enlarge the infarct.

evidence.snippet: The principal mechanisms discussed include oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction, calcium overload and ion homeostasis imbalance, inflammatory responses, with particular focus on the NLRP3 inflammasome and cytokine pathways, and multiple forms of cell death (apoptosis, necroptosis, pyroptosis, and autophagy).
evidence.explanation: Enumerates the oxidative-stress, calcium-overload, NLRP3-inflammasome, and multi-modal cell-death mechanisms attributed to MIRI in this node.

evidence.snippet: underscoring its potential to contribute substantially to the final infarct size, up to 50%.
evidence.explanation: Independent review corroborating that MIRI can contribute up to 50% of the final infarct size.

steps/2.description: Restoration of coronary blood flow (by primary PCI or fibrinolysis) is essential to salvage ischemic myocardium but paradoxically inflicts additional damage — myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI) — that can account for up to half of the final infarct size. Reperfusion drives a burst of reactive oxygen species, cytosolic and mitochondrial calcium overload, and sustained opening of the mitochondrial permeability transition pore (MPTP) with collapse of the mitochondrial membrane potential and cessation of ATP production, together with endothelial dysfunction, NLRP3 inflammasome activation, and multiple regulated cell-death programs (apoptosis, necroptosis, pyroptosis, ferroptosis) and dysregulated autophagy.

evidence.snippet: After infarction, massive cardiomyocyte death releases a broad range of damage-associated molecular patterns that initiate both myocardial and systemic inflammatory responses.
evidence.explanation: Evidences DAMP release from dying cardiomyocytes as the trigger of the post-infarction inflammatory response.

evidence.snippet: Expansion and diversification of cardiac macrophages in the infarcted heart play a major role in the clearance of the infarct from dead cells and the subsequent stimulation of reparative pathways.
evidence.explanation: Supports the role of cardiac macrophage expansion in clearing the infarct and initiating repair.

evidence.snippet: Efferocytosis triggers the induction and release of anti-inflammatory mediators that restrain the inflammatory reaction and set the stage for the activation of reparative fibroblasts and vascular cells.
evidence.explanation: Evidences the efferocytosis-driven switch from inflammation to fibroblast-mediated repair that this node describes.

evidence.snippet: Myocardial infarction (MI) sets off a complex inflammatory cascade that is crucial for effective cardiac healing and scar formation.
evidence.explanation: Corroborates that the post-MI inflammatory cascade is essential for cardiac healing and scar formation.

evidence.snippet: Yet, if this response becomes excessive or uncontrolled, it can lead to cardiovascular complications.
evidence.explanation: Supports that a dysregulated post-MI inflammatory response drives adverse cardiovascular outcomes.

steps/3.description: Massive cardiomyocyte death releases damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs/alarmins) that engage pattern-recognition receptors (TLRs, NLRs), driving cytokine (IL-1, TNF-alpha, IL-6) and chemokine (CCL2) production and recruitment of neutrophils and monocytes. Expansion and diversification of cardiac macrophages clears dead cells; efferocytosis then triggers anti-inflammatory mediators (IL-10, TGF-beta) that restrain inflammation and activate reparative fibroblasts and vascular cells. This tightly regulated inflammatory-to-reparative transition is essential for healing, but an excessive or unresolved response promotes adverse outcomes.

evidence.snippet: The cardiac fibroblast-to-myofibroblast differentiation and extracellular matrix collagen deposition are the hallmarks of cardiac fibrosis, which are modulated by multiple signaling pathways
evidence.explanation: Evidences fibroblast-to-myofibroblast conversion and ECM collagen deposition as the hallmarks of post-MI cardiac fibrosis.

evidence.snippet: Cardiac fibrosis plays an indispensable role in cardiac tissue homeostasis and repair after myocardial infarction (MI).
evidence.explanation: Supports that fibrosis is central to tissue repair and remodeling after MI.
